articles.title: Eleições em Israel: urnas são fechadas, e pesquisas de boca de urna indicam impasse | G1
articles.standfirst: País renovará o Parlamento, que indica o primeiro-ministro. Pesquisas mostram que nem coalizão do premiê, nem oposição têm maioria suficiente para formar governo. Netanyahu aposta no apoio popular a guerras, mas pode deixar o poder e enfrentar a Justiça.
articles.summary: País renovará o Parlamento, que indica o primeiro-ministro. Pesquisas mostram que nem coalizão do premiê, nem oposição têm maioria suficiente para formar governo. Netanyahu aposta no apoio popular a guerras, mas pode deixar o poder e enfrentar a Justiça.
articles.body:
Benjamin Netanyahu e Gadi Eisenkot — Foto: Yonatan Sindel/Pool via REUTERS e REUTERS/Shir Torem

As urnas fecharam em Israel , que teve suas primeiras eleições gerais no país desde o início da guerra na Faixa de Gaza nesta terça-feira (27). Segundo as pesquisas de boca de urna divulgadas pelas principais redes de televisão, o pleito terminou com um aparente impasse.

Os levantamentos indicam que nem o primeiro-ministro Benjamin Netanyahu nem seu principal adversário, Gadi Eisenkot , devem conquistar maioria no Parlamento, ou 61 das 120 cadeiras.

O bloco de oposição lidera por uma margem estreita, conquistando entre 52 e 53 das vagas

A coalizão governista de Netanyahu, por sua vez, teria obtido 50 acentos .

Dois partidos árabes israelenses poderiam conquistar um número recorde de cadeiras: 17 ou 18, segundo as mesmas pesquisas.

O partido Ra'am (Lista Árabe Unida, de orientação islâmica moderada), liderado por Mansur Abbas, deverá obter sete cadeiras

A Lista Unificada de (extrema esquerda) conquistaria dez ou 11 assentos .

O resultado pode favorecer Netanyahu e permitir que ele permaneça no poder como chefe de um governo interino enquanto os partidos tentam formar uma coalizão . A apuração final pode levar dias, e a fragmentação política do país dá às legendas menores um papel decisivo na formação de uma maioria.

Com a popularidade em baixa e alvo de processos na Justiça israelense e um de mandado de prisão internacional , Netanyahu tenta se reeleger. No entanto, chega às eleições em desvantagem e corre o risco de perder o posto, embora nenhum outro partido mostre força suficiente para tomar o cargo.

➡️ Os israelenses foram às urnas nesta terça para eleger os 120 deputados que compõem o Knesset , como é chamado o Parlamento israelense.

Em Israel, um partido precisa ocupar pelo menos 61 assentos na Casa para obter maioria e, então, indicar quem será o primeiro-ministro. Nenhum partido alcançou a bancada e, por isso, a formação de coalizões é necessária para governar o país.

A votação registrou participação recorde e foi a primeira eleição desde os ataques liderados pelo Hamas em 7 de outubro de 2023. Os eleitores avaliaram a atuação de Netanyahu durante os conflitos que se seguiram em Gaza, no Líbano e no Irã.

As políticas da coalizão de direita do primeiro-ministro dividiram a população israelense e aprofundaram o isolamento internacional do país. Netanyahu, porém, apresentou-se durante a campanha como o líder mais preparado para enfrentar os adversários de Israel.

Um dos partidos da aliança é a sigla da extrema direita Otzma Yehudit, do polêmico Itamar Ben-Gvir, atual ministro de Segurança Nacional de Netanyahu. Principal braço da coalizão do governo israelense, a legenda não deve chegar a 9 assentos.

O líder do partido Yashar, Gadi Eisenkot, também ex-chefe das Forças Armadas de Israel, agita bandeira após falar em comício em Tel Aviv, em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: David Goldman/ AP

Aos 77 anos, Netanyahu ocupou o cargo de primeiro-ministro por quase 19 dos últimos 30 anos e sobreviveu a diversas crises políticas. Ele chegou à eleição sob acusações de corrupção que enfrenta há anos e nega, além de críticas pelas falhas de inteligência que permitiram o ataque do Hamas em 2023. Na ocasião, militantes mataram 1.200 pessoas e fizeram 251 reféns.

Eisenkot, de 66 anos, é um ex-chefe militar de perfil linha-dura que perdeu um filho e dois sobrinhos na guerra em Gaza. Ele se tornou o principal adversário de Netanyahu ao destacar sua experiência na área de segurança e, ao mesmo tempo, apresentar-se como uma alternativa de centro na política interna.

O ex-comandante entrou na política há apenas quatro anos e integrou o gabinete de guerra de Netanyahu após os ataques do Hamas. Oito meses depois, deixou o governo e criticou a liderança do primeiro-ministro.

Se nenhum dos dois conseguir reunir apoio suficiente para formar uma maioria parlamentar, Israel poderá enfrentar longas negociações para a formação de um governo ou a convocação de novas eleições.

Foi o que aconteceu alguns anos atrás, quando Israel fez cinco eleições, até que, no fim de 2022, Netanyahu garantiu a maioria com uma decisão controversa.

Na ocasião, ele topou aliança com o partido de Ben Gvir, da extrema direita, em uma parceria vista por vários especialistas como um dos fatores propulsores da guerra.

Isso porque Ben Gvir, que virou ministro, fez forte pressão para que Netanyahu sufocasse palestinos na Cisjordânia, permitindo novos assentamentos ilegais de judeus. O ministro também já defendeu a ocupação total da Faixa de Gaza.

Para tentar capitanear eleitores indecisos, Netanyahu insiste no discurso da guerra, que ainda tem apoio expressivo dentro de Israel. Embora o conflito em Gaza tenha desgastado internamente o premiê, a guerra que ele trava contra o Irã renovou o apoio popular a ofensivas israelenses .

👉 As eleições são as primeiras desde que o Hamas invadiu Israel , há três anos, em uma matança que deixou mais de 1.200 mortos e fez com que Netanyahu declarasse guerra ao grupo terrorista, financiado pelo Irã. O conflito, que só na Faixa de Gaza deixou cerca de 75 mil palestinos mortos, se alastrou pelo Oriente Médio e sofreu intervenção dos EUA, aliado de Israel e em guerra aberta contra Teerã.

Para o pleito, Netanyahu também tentou capitalizar a parceria com Trump , mesmo que a aliança tenha se enfraquecido neste ano por discordâncias dos dois sobre ataques ao Irã.

Mas a narrativa bélica foi a maior aposta do premiê israelense para tentar angariar mais votos. Ao longo da campanha, ele tem insistido que a guerra no Irã é a última chance de Israel de combater inimigos contrários à existência do país.

👉 Na segunda-feira (26), a imprensa israelense relatou que Netanyahu pressionou as Forças Armadas para deflagrar uma escalada contra Teerã . O gabinete do premiê negou a informação oficialmente, mas Netanyahu, ainda de acordo com a imprensa israelense, prometeu demitir lideranças militares por conta de uma suposta resistência a um ataque horas antes das eleições.

Diante da notícia, a oposição acusou o premiê de colocar em risco a estabilidade regional em prol de sua própria sobrevivência política. Gadi Eisenkot, seu principal rival, pediu ao premiê não “ousar colocar seus próprios interesses políticos acima da segurança do Estado”.

Em uma publicação no X, Eisenkot escreveu: “Netanyahu, estou de olho em você”.

A oposição também defende que o premiê seja responsabilizado pelas falhas relacionadas ao ataque de 7 de outubro. Já apoiadores afirmam que Netanyahu conduziu o país na superação de seu momento mais difícil.

Pesquisas apontam que os eleitores estão divididos entre os dois argumentos .

Mas, apesar das críticas, os principais rivais do premiê possuem abordagens semelhantes em relação à segurança regional de Israel, tanto no que diz respeito a Gaza quanto ao Irã.

Netanyahu em campanha, às vésperas das eleições nacionais de Israel, em Tel Aviv — Foto: REUTERS/Itai Ron

articles.title: Brasileira morre na França enquanto dormia durante viagem a Paris | G1
articles.standfirst: Goiana fazia faculdade on-line de Gestão Financeira e falava italiano fluente. Anna Júlia morava na Itália e estava passeando com amigas em Paris.
articles.summary: Brasileira morre na França: Anna Júlia Barros Silva tinha 24 anos, vivia na Itália e sofria de uma síndrome que causa trombose, segundo relato de sua mãe ao g1.
articles.body:
Anna Júlia Barros Silva, de 24 anos, morreu na França — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Patricia

A brasileira Anna Júlia Barros Silva, de 24 anos, morreu enquanto dormia durante viagem de passeio na França. Segundo a mãe da jovem, Patricia Antônia de Barros, a filha estava com outras duas amigas e pode ter passado mal durante a noite. Anna Júlia é natural de Anápolis, na região central do estado, e morava na Itália há um ano e seis meses.

Patricia disse ao g1 que Anna Júlia sempre foi muito aventureira, gostava de sair e tinha vontade de morar fora. Foi trabalhar para conquistar sua independência. Atualmente, a jovem trabalhava e morava em Roma, capital da Itália, e também cursava faculdade online de Gestão Financeira.

Segundo a mãe da jovem, Anna Júlia tinha uma doença chamada Síndrome do Anticorpo Antifosfolipídeo (SAF) que é uma pré-disposição para trombose e tomava anticoagulante com regularidade por causa dessa condição.

"Em janeiro do ano passado ela ficou internada muitos dias na Unidade de Tratamento Intensivo (UTI). Ela quase faleceu por conta da trombose, então, ela tomava anticoagulante", afirmou.

Anna Júlia morreu no sábado (24) e chegou a conversar com a mãe na noite antes de dormir. Patrícia contou que a filha precisava tomar remédio para conseguir dormir e que falou com ela pela última vez na noite de sexta-feira (23), depois que Anna Júlia havia chegado de um passeio com outras três amigas. Na manhã seguinte, a família recebeu a notícia da morte de Anna Júlia pela polícia.

"Ela passou mal dormindo, a amiga do lado não percebeu. Quando elas acordaram, foram chamar todo mundo para se arrumar e seguir o roteiro do passeio e perceberam que ela não estava acordando e que ela estava sem vida. Aí já acionaram a polícia", disse a mãe.

articles.title: Criminosos invadem UBS em Natal, atiram e roubam arma de vigilante | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois homens chegaram de moto à unidade, renderam o profissional e fugiram com o revólver calibre 38. Os atendimentos previstos para a tarde desta terça-feira (27) foram reagendados.
articles.summary: Dois homens chegaram de moto à unidade, renderam o profissional e fugiram com o revólver calibre 38. Os atendimentos previstos para a tarde desta terça(27) foram reagendados.
articles.body:
Disparo atingiu equipamento da unidade de saúde — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV

Dois homens invadiram a Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) Dix-Sept Rosado, em Natal , na manhã desta terça-feira (27), atiraram contra um vigilante e roubaram o revólver calibre 38 que estava com ele. Ninguém ficou ferido.

A Secretaria Municipal de Saúde (SMS) informou que os atendimentos previstos para a tarde desta terça-feira na UBS foram suspensos e reagendados.

Segundo o relato do vigilante, a dupla chegou ao local por volta das 9h, em uma motocicleta, pelo portão de acesso à Avenida Nevaldo Rocha. Um dos homens atirou dentro da unidade. O disparo atingiu um equipamento de refrigeração de água da unidade.

Após o tiro, um dos suspeitos rendeu o vigilante, enquanto o outro pegou a arma dele. Na saída, os dois ainda deram um tiro para cima. Em seguida, fugiram na motocicleta.

A Guarda Municipal foi acionada e prestou apoio no local. O vigilante foi levado à delegacia para prestar depoimento.

Atendimento foi suspenso na unidade — Foto: Victor Eduardo/Inter TV

A SMS informou que os atendimentos previstos para a tarde desta terça-feira na UBS foram suspensos e precisaram ser reagendados.

Segundo informações repassadas por moradores da região, a unidade já havia registrado outros casos de insegurança nas últimas semanas, incluindo o furto de equipamentos de ar-condicionado instalados na parte externa do prédio.

articles.title: Influenciadora diz que cancelou viagem para resort na BA após eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo foi publicado após anúncio da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
articles.summary: Vídeo foi publicado após anúncio da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).
articles.body:
A influenciadora Aline Guimarães disse que desistiu de passar férias em um resort na Bahia após o resultado das eleições. Moradora do Espírito Santo, ela tem mais de 40 mil seguidores na redes sociais, onde produz conteúdo sobre maternidade, moda e compras.

O vídeo foi publicado na segunda-feira (26) após o anúncio da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ).

"Cancelamos a nossa viagem para o Nordeste. Sim, cancelamos, gente. Iríamos para um resort na Bahia. Cancelamos. Não vou mais pisar na Bahia, não vou levar o nosso suado dinheiro daqui para gastar lá", afirmou.

Em seguida, Aline Guimarães pediu para que os seguidores fizessem sugestões de resorts no Sul ou no Sudeste.

“Quem tiver sugestões de resort no Sul ou no Sudeste, aceito indicações”.

Influenciadora diz que cancelou viagem para resort na Bahia após eleições — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Com a repercussão nas redes sociais, a influenciadora comentou a repercussão nesta segunda-feira (27).

Com a repercussão do vídeo nas redes sociais, Aline Guimarães voltou a comentar o assunto nesta terça-feira (27). Em uma nova gravação, a influenciadora afirmou que ela e o marido têm liberdade para escolher o destino das férias e negou ter cometido preconceito contra os nordestinos ou contra a Bahia.

“Gente, vamos lá. Primeiro, eu vou para onde eu quiser. O dinheiro é meu, o dinheiro é do meu marido, então a gente vai para onde a gente quiser”, disse.

A influenciadora também afirmou que não pretende mais viajar para a Bahia e criticou as reações ao vídeo. “Não cometi nenhum preconceito contra os nordestinos, contra a Bahia, mas a gente não quer ir mais, pronto. Quero outras indicações. Não cometi nenhum crime. Aí o povo fica procurando confusão”, declarou.

Aline ainda comentou que perdeu seguidores após a publicação e disse que silenciou algumas pessoas nas redes sociais durante o período de repercussão do caso. Segundo ela, entre essas pessoas estão amigos que apoiam o PT.

“Tem vários amigos petistas, tem várias pessoas que eu sei que pararam de me seguir. Alguns que eu gosto, que não queria parar de seguir, eu silenciei. Depois que passar esse período vou voltar a ver os stories, mas eu não sou extremista, eu falei que não queria ir à Bahia”, afirmou.

articles.title: Operador de caixa denuncia agressão em terminal de ônibus de Sorocaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Guilherme de Oliveira Faria, de 26 anos, registrou um boletim de ocorrência por uma 'ombrada' que teria recebido e suspeita ter sido vítima de homofobia.
articles.summary: O operador de caixa Guilherme de Oliveira Faria alega ter sido agredido por um motorista de ônibus de Sorocaba (SP). O rapaz suspeita ter sido vítima de homofobia.
articles.body:
Um operador de caixa de Sorocaba (SP) denunciou ter sido agredido por um motorista de ônibus municipal. Guilherme de Oliveira Faria, de 26 anos, tentava tirar a segunda via do vale-transporte e diz que suspeita ter sido vítima de homofobia. A Urbes, empresa que gerencia e fiscaliza o trânsito e o transporte coletivo, disse que apura o ocorrido.

Faria divulgou um relato sobre o episódio nas redes sociais e afirmou que também registrou um boletim de ocorrência pela agressão.

De acordo com o operador de caixa, no dia 20 de outubro, por volta do meio-dia, ele embarcou em um ônibus da linha 11 - Manchester/Ipiranga e disse ao motorista que precisava ir ao terminal solicitar a segunda via do vale-transporte, que tinha perdido. Para isso, apresentou o documento e uma carta comprobatória, sendo autorizado a viajar na frente.

Ainda segundo Faria, quando chegou ao terminal, foi abordado “de forma muito agressiva” por um funcionário e explicou que desejava tirar a segunda via do vale-transporte e regularizar o pagamento da passagem.

“Assim que eu desci do ônibus, fui abordado de maneira muito agressiva já pelo funcionário do terminal. Tentei me explicar, mostrar para ele diversas vezes o documento da solicitação que eu tinha, mas em nenhum momento ele quis me ouvir. Pelo contrário, ele disse: ‘se você não tem dinheiro pra pagar o passe, você não deveria tentar explicar para mim, e sim para uma assistente social’”, afirmou o operador de caixa.

Seguindo em direção ao escritório, Faria diz que parou para ir ao banheiro e foi seguido pelo motorista e o outro funcionário. No boletim de ocorrência, o rapaz relatou ter sido chamado de “vagabundo” e viu o motorista avançar contra ele.

“Eu vi que eles estavam me seguindo e eles me coagiram lá dentro, começaram a me xingar e a discussão foi ficando cada vez mais forte. Assim que eu saí, ele foi atrás de mim e me deu uma ombrada. Uma senhora tentou apartar a briga e eu já estava me sentindo envergonhado. Tentei me explicar e eles me interrompiam e me humilhavam o tempo todo”.

Na ocorrência, Faria contou que, logo depois, outros três indivíduos, que não trabalhavam no terminal, se aproximaram e passaram a agredi-lo com socos. Ele foi socorrido por duas funcionárias, que separaram a briga.

“Até então, eu não tinha entendido nada, eu só queria resolver e sair dali, fugir. Assim que eu entrei na sala, eu expliquei para as funcionárias o que tinha acontecido e só conseguia repetir que eu era trabalhador e que não faria aquilo para prejudicar ninguém. Ela entendeu a situação e disse que o que tinha acontecido não era por conta do passe, mas porque eu sou homossexual”, frisou.

Faria disse, ainda, que uma testemunha relatou a ele ter ouvido o motorista chamá-lo de “viado”. “Ninguém que sai de casa buscando uma vida melhor merece passar por isso”, destacou.

Após o episódio, Faria contou ter pedido um afastamento de cinco dias do trabalho para cuidar da saúde mental. Ele está sendo acompanhado por um psicólogo.

Guilherme de Oliveira Faria, de 26 anos, registrou um boletim de ocorrência por agressão em terminal de ônibus de Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Divulgação

A Urbes - Trânsito e Transporte foi questionada sobre o episódio e, por meio de nota, informou que apura o ocorrido no terminal e colabora com as autoridades, fornecendo dados e imagens para ajudar na investigação.

“A Urbes repudia qualquer ato de agressão, hostilidade ou discriminação e cobrou das empresas operadoras para que todos os usuários sejam tratados com respeito e segurança”.

Questionada sobre a segurança do terminal, por conta das agressões posteriores relatadas pelo operador de caixa, a empresa pública afirmou que há patrulhamento feito pelas equipes da guarda Civil Municipal (GCM), mas que, na ocasião, não houve constatação do caso pela guarnição, situação que motivou reforço na vigilância.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo Vale do Paraíba: El Niño traz chuva em novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Meteorologista explica que excesso de nebulosidade e chuva dificulta a elevação das temperaturas; períodos de calor devem ser curtos em novembro.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo para o Vale do Paraíba em novembro indica chuva frequente e pouco sol sob influência do El Niño, com raros períodos de calor na região.
articles.body:
Quem espera a chegada do calor típico da primavera deve ter que esperar um pouco mais no Vale do Paraíba e região.

O excesso de nebulosidade e a frequência de chuva têm mantido as temperaturas mais amenas na região, e a previsão para novembro é de um cenário semelhante, com períodos de calor, mas sem uma sequência prolongada de dias quentes.

Segundo a meteorologista Josélia Pegorim, da Climatempo, o comportamento do tempo está relacionado às mudanças na circulação dos ventos provocadas pelo El Niño, fenômeno climático que influencia as condições meteorológicas no Brasil.

"A previsão já era de excesso de nebulosidade e excesso de chuva para o mês de outubro e, justamente por isso, a temperatura não iria subir muito", afirmou.

Cidade de São José dos Campos nesta terça-feira (27). — Foto: Monika Moretto

Por que está chovendo tanto e fazendo menos calor?

De acordo com Josélia, o excesso de nuvens e a chuva frequente no Vale do Paraíba começaram a ganhar força em setembro, quando diversas frentes frias passaram pela costa de São Paulo.

Mesmo depois da passagem desses sistemas, a circulação de ar marítimo transporta umidade para o leste paulista, favorecendo a formação de nuvens.

"Quando passa a frente fria, entra uma circulação de ar marítimo que injeta muita umidade no leste do estado de São Paulo. Então, isso produz uma quantidade de nuvens muito grande, mesmo depois que já passou a chuva intensa", explicou.

Em outubro, além das frentes frias, outros sistemas meteorológicos contribuíram para manter o tempo instável na região. Com a presença frequente de nuvens e chuva, a incidência de sol diminui e as temperaturas têm mais dificuldade para subir.

"Um outubro normal é até um outubro quente, mas, por causa desse excesso de nuvens e chuva, que é um efeito do El Niño, a temperatura não está subindo muito", disse a meteorologista.

Jardim Oswaldo Cruz, em São José dos Campos. — Foto: Cíntia Garcia/Rede Vanguarda

A previsão é de que novembro também tenha episódios frequentes de chuva e nebulosidade no Vale do Paraíba, o que deve dificultar a elevação das temperaturas. Embora o mês costume ser mais quente do que outubro, a expectativa é de que os períodos de calor sejam curtos.

"Alguns picos de calor, mas não contem com períodos prolongados de sol e calor, não", alertou Josélia.

Segundo ela, a região poderá registrar dias com temperaturas mais elevadas, mas a expectativa é de que esses períodos não durem muito. "Vai ser difícil a gente ter uma semana inteira, por exemplo, com calor em torno de 30 graus em novembro", afirmou.

A última semana de outubro também deve ter mudanças nas condições do tempo. De acordo com a meteorologista, uma nova frente fria deve chegar a São Paulo no domingo (1º de novembro).

Depois da passagem do sistema, a tendência é de mais dias nublados e com temperaturas amenas. No início de novembro, as temperaturas poderão subir novamente, mas o período de calor deve ser curto.

El Niño deve continuar influenciando o clima

Segundo Josélia Pegorim, a influência do El Niño sobre o clima brasileiro deve continuar durante a primavera e o verão, podendo se estender até parte do outono do próximo ano.

"Então, o estado de São Paulo, junto com o Paraná e Mato Grosso do Sul, estão tendo dias com muita instabilidade", explicou.

A meteorologista destacou que o excesso de nebulosidade e chuva observado em outubro faz parte de um cenário diferente do que costuma ser esperado para o período.

"É uma situação atípica para outubro, mas está dentro do previsto para este outubro", afirmou.

A expectativa para novembro, portanto, é de um mês com alternância entre períodos de chuva, nebulosidade e dias mais quentes, sem predominância prolongada de sol e calor.

articles.title: Men sexually assaulted Philip Young's wife after online ad, court told
articles.summary: Four men stand trial after the woman's ex-husband has pleaded guilty to drugging and raping her.
articles.body:
Four men sexually assaulted a woman after her then-husband drugged her and advertised her on Craigslist, Grindr and swinging websites, a court has been told.

Norman Macksoni, 48, Richard Wilkins, 62, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, and Mohammed Hassan, 38, are on trial at Winchester Crown Court after pleading not guilty to sexual offences against Joanne Young.

They are charged jointly with her ex-husband Philip Young, 50, a former Conservative councillor, who has admitted to drugging and raping her over 13 years.

As the trial began, prosecutor Sarah Jones KC told the jury: "This case is about whether it is ever reasonable to have sex with an unknown woman without checking with her first."

Warning: This story contains distressing details

Joanne Young, who has waived her right to anonymity, told police that to her knowledge she had a "fairly normal" and "always monogamous" sex life with her husband.

But on one occasion in 2023, she said she had woken up with restraints and a blindfold on while a man was carrying out a sexual act on her.

Jones told the jury Joanne had believed her husband was performing the sexual act on her when in reality he was "stage managing another unknown person" who was "taking his place without her knowledge".

Jones told the jury Young had advertised Joanne online, seeking "strangers to come and sleep with his wife".

"He presented it as a kink for both of them, but there was no information from Joanne herself to support this and the photos he posted of her to advertise his offer showed her inanimate and tied to the bed blindfolded," Jones told the court.

"The nightcap they shared, it appeared, would be used to plunge her into a state where anything could be done to her by whoever answered and she would be unaware or unable to remember."

Sanderson-Doyle, of Swindon, denies sexual assault by penetration and sexual touching during an incident in 2016.

The court was told he had responded to an advert on Craigslist.

Jones said there was a video which showed Sanderson-Doyle wearing a balaclava while touching Joanne, who was shackled to a bed.

The video later showed Joanne protesting and Sanderson-Doyle apologising before continuing to touch her.

Jones told the jury Sanderson-Doyle had made "no further enquiry" that what he was doing was "welcome or acceptable" and had only stopped when Young said "No, let go".

The court heard this had prompted Young to stop filming before showing Sanderson-Doyle the door.

Jones said Sanderson-Doyle had said he believed Joanne had consented and he thought the married couple were "trying to live out whatever their kink" was.

Macksoni, of Sharnbrook, Bedfordshire, has denied one count of rape in 2017.

Jones told the jury Macksoni had been filmed having sex with Young, who was blindfolded and shackled to the bed and whose "less than wholehearted" participation" was "wholly akin to what you might expect if someone were drugged".

The court heard the video showed Young reassuring his then-wife, whose speech was "slurred and confused" that she was not being recorded.

Jones told the jury Macksoni had "not uttered one word to Joanne Young through the almost seven minutes of recording that he is in the room with her".

Jones said when interviewed by police, Macksoni had said he believed Joanne and Young had consented.

Wilkins, of Toothill, Swindon, Wiltshire, has pleaded not guilty to one count of rape and one of assault by penetration in 2016.

Jones told the jury a video showed Wilkins touching Joanne "without any attempt to rouse or have a word with her".

Naked, blindfolded and shackled to the bed, Joanne can be heard snoring and is "quite evidently asleep", the court was told.

Wilkins exchanged whispers with Young about what to do, before penetrating her and shooting a "triumphant grin" at him over his shoulder, the court heard.

"The notion of checking with the woman who is so out of it she is snoring never seems to enter the minds of either," Jones told the jury, adding: "They have no interest in her consent."

Jones said had Wilkins denied the offences and had answered no comment in police interview.

Mohammed Hassan, of Swindon, has pleaded not guilty to one count of sexual touching in 2023.

There is no video evidence of the incident, but Hassan was traced through messages with Young on Grindr inviting him to come over to the couple's home where Joanne would be tied up and "falling asleep", the court heard.

Joanne recalled becoming aware there was another man in the room when she believed a sexual act was being carried out by her husband, the court heard.

The jury was told Young had apologised in a message to Hassan the following day, saying his wife had "freaked out".

Jones said Hassan had denied the charge and did not answer questions in police interview.

Jones said the men could not have reasonably believed at the time that Joanne was consenting because of the state she was in and the circumstances.

"They took what her husband was offering out to them without ever checking for a second with the woman herself whether she was OK with it," she told the jury.

"They did not ask because they did not want it to be unambiguously clear Joanne was unaware of what was happening and unable to express her true thoughts and feelings.

"They wanted to enact their fantasy and Phil Young's fantasy and they did not care about Joanne's feelings at all."

Young has admitted 14 counts of voyeurism, 11 of rape, 11 of administering a substance with intent, seven of assault by penetration, four of sexual assault and one of publishing an obscene article.

The former councillor also published more than 500 intimate images and videos of his ex-wife and recorded her doing private acts for his own sexual gratification without her consent between 2010 and 2024.

A sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.

Young and Hamilton will be sentenced at the end of the trial, which is expected to last up to four weeks.

articles.title: Pakistan’s top court upholds Christian man’s death sentence for blasphemy
articles.summary: Pakistan’s Supreme Court upheld a Christian man’s death sentence for blasphemy in a historic ruling that advocates warn could have far-reaching consequences.
articles.body: Shock and anger greeted the Pakistani Supreme Court's decision to uphold the conviction and death sentence of a Christian man accused of blasphemy against the Prophet Muhammad. Supporters say the decision has far-reaching implications for human rights in Pakistan and for the country's standing on the international stage. The Open Doors 2026 World Watch List included the Asian nation in its top 10 list of countries where Christians face the most extreme persecution. CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), told Fox News Digital the case against brothers Amoon and Qaisar Ayub began in 2014. AMERICANS TRAVEL TO PAKISTAN TO FREE CHRISTIANS TRAPPED IN MODERN-DAY SLAVERY: 'GOD'S HAND WAS IN IT' Qaisar was arrested after a WordPress site displayed the Ayub brothers’ contact information and shared content that insulted the Prophet Muhammad. Amoon was arrested the following year. Heil says that in the 12 years of legal wrangling that followed, the Pakistani legal system has never presented evidence proving that either brother was truly affiliated with the offending WordPress blog site. The ACLJ, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), began representing Amoon shortly after his arrest in 2015. Both brothers were sentenced to death in 2018. They unsuccessfully sought appeal in the Lahore High Court in 2022. After a continuation at the Supreme Court in 2025, Qaisar asked the OLA to represent him. Following years of arguments and 13 postponed hearings, an Oct. 7 verdict from the Supreme Court saw Amoon acquitted after some 10 years in prison, while Qaisar’s conviction and death sentence was upheld. Heil said a threatening atmosphere now attends many blasphemy hearings, where she says "mobs" commonly show up in courtrooms. In one trial, she said a mob filmed themselves saying that "if the judge does not enforce death by hanging, we will kill him by our own hands." She said another video shows a prominent lawyer involved in numerous blasphemy cases celebrating the 15-year journey that led to Qaisar’s sentencing. A translation of the description reads, "There is only one punishment for one who insults the Prophet: The death penalty for Qaisar Ayub." Heil said the precedent set by the Supreme Court’s decision could impact "every single person that is sitting in prison right now on blasphemy charges," which includes at least three OLA clients. Other Christian men facing death include Shahzad Masih, who was 16 years old when he was accused of blasphemy in 2017. He was sentenced to death five years later. His appeals have repeatedly been postponed since 2022. Intizar Masih is awaiting trial for a blasphemous post he is said to have shared on WhatsApp in 2023. Ahsan Masih was accused of posting blasphemous content to TikTok in 2023, and was sentenced to death the following year. His appeal hearings have also been postponed. The OLA plans to file a review petition with the Supreme Court as early as this week, addressing the lack of evidence convicting Qaisar. They also plan to reach out directly to the Government of Pakistan to request support, including a presidential pardon for Qaisar. Heil said she finds it "very strange" for a country posturing itself as a "more tolerant" negotiator between world powers in the ongoing conflict in Iran to fail to protect the religious freedoms of its people. CHRISTIAN FARMING COMMUNITIES UNDER SIEGE AS US REPORT NAMES FULANI MILITANTS NIGERIA'S DEADLIEST THREAT The Pakistani Embassy in Washington, D.C., did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about the possibility of a presidential pardon for Qaisar, or whether the Supreme Court’s decision could impact Pakistan’s perception in the West, or if justice can prevail in courtrooms mobbed with threatening onlookers. A State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the U.S. "is concerned about religious freedom in Pakistan and throughout the world" and "we regularly discuss this concern with Pakistan, as we would with any country." Heil said the ACLJ has requested that Morris Tidball-Binz, the United Nations special rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, intercede on Qaisar’s behalf. Tidball-Binz did not respond to Fox News Digital’s questions about whether he held concerns about the precedent set by the Supreme Court upholding Qaisar’s conviction. The Human Rights Council secretariat provided a letter that Tidball-Binz and other U.N. officials wrote to the Government of Pakistan in September 2025, emphasizing their concerns about the cases of the Ayub brothers and Shahazad Masih. It stated, "Without making any judgment as to the accuracy of the information made available to us, we would like to express our grave concern about the imposition of the mandatory death penalty for blasphemy related charges against Mr. Shahzad Masih, Mr. Qaiser Ayub and Mr. Amoon Ayub, despite an apparent lack of conclusive evidence against them for acts and for offenses which do not qualify as ‘most serious crimes.’" The U.N. officials concluded, "If the above allegations prove to be accurate, they would be in contravention of Mr. Shahazad Masih´s, Mr. Qaiser Ayub’s and Mr. Amoon Ayub’s rights to life, not to be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, not to be deprived arbitrarily of their liberty and to be afforded fair proceedings before an independent and impartial tribunal, to freedom of thought, conscience and religion or belief, the right to express their opinion in a peaceful manner and the right to be equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law without any discrimination." The Government of Pakistan responded earlier this year, and outlined how "Under Pakistan's Constitution, such matters fall within the judicial domain, and the Executive is constitutionally prohibited from intervening in individual cases." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Heil said that while Amoon has been spared from the death penalty, their work is ongoing to keep him safe from reprisals.

articles.title: Finland’s Stubb and Norway PM call Putin in break with previous European stance
articles.summary: The leaders of Finland and Norway initiated a direct call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday morning amid broader diplomatic efforts to wind down Russia’s yearslong war with Ukraine. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre noted in a joint press release that they did not speak on behalf of…
articles.body:
The leaders of Finland and Norway initiated a direct call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday morning amid broader diplomatic efforts to wind down Russia’s yearslong war with Ukraine.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre noted in a joint press release that they did not speak on behalf of “Europe as a whole” in this conversation but only as the leaders of their respective countries.

Stubb called the discussion “frank and substantive,” noting that both Finland and Norway share a border with Russia.

“The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions,” the Finnish leader said in a statement.

The conversation comes ahead of planned trilateral talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi next month.

“The war comes with enormous human and material costs,” Støre said following the call with Putin. “The suffering and destruction will impact generations. In the call we stressed the importance of de-escalation.”

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed the conversation to Russian news agency TASS and said the European leaders acknowledged “the importance of respecting international maritime law and the principle of freedom of navigation” during their call with Putin.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday in a social media post that he also spoke with Stubb and Støre afterward and he thanked them for providing a “detailed briefing” of their conversation with the Russian leader.

“Alex and Jonas made it clear to the Russian leader that real de-escalatory steps are needed regarding our energy and infrastructure,” Zelensky wrote, adding that they discussed the upcoming November negotiations and strengthening Ukraine’s European partnerships.

Several European partners criticized the phone call later Tuesday. Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen told Denmark’s TV 2 on Tuesday she was “very skeptical” about the negotiation effort and noting that it was “not coordinated” with the rest of Europe.

“I think you should keep Europe together instead of going solo,” Frederiksen told the outlet.

“I actually don’t know what the two countries think you can achieve with this,” the prime minister continued. “In the past, we have also emphasised in clear messages from the rest of Europe that when others have gone solo and, for example, travelled to Moscow, it is important that we Europeans join forces.”

articles.title: Bill Maher, Justine Bateman compare far-left policies to 'The Purge in real life'
articles.summary: Justine Bateman and Bill Maher likened the DSA platform to horror movie "The Purge" in real life, questioning plans to abolish police, prisons, and the Senate.
articles.body: Actress Justine Bateman and comedian Bill Maher compared far-left policies — specifically, the Democratic Socialists of America's (DSA) goals — to "The Purge" in real life on Monday, questioning why critics of those policies are expected to "bow down." "What's the endgame?" Bateman asked of the socialist policies of the DSA during an appearance on Maher's "Club Random" podcast. "Let's say you get everything you wanted. Let's say everything on that list. You get the whole thing. The whole thing. I mean, first of all, I can tell you for sure, anybody could tell you, you haven't thought this through." Maher called it "cloud cuckoo land" as Bateman began comparing the proposals to the movie "The Purge." DSA CO-CHAIR PUSHES BACK ON SOVIET UNION COMPARISONS, WANTS PRISONS TO BE 'LESS NECESSARY' "You've got ‘The Purge’ in real life because you have no jails and no – everybody better have a gun. Don't touch the Second Amendment. Everybody needs a gun if you're going to have that," she said. "I’ve said the same exact thing. It’s ‘The Purge.’ It’s ‘The Purge.’" "The Purge" is a movie about a government-sanctioned, 12-hour annual event where all crime, including murder, is completely legal. BILL MAHER WARNS DEMOCRATS STILL HAVEN'T 'RENOUNCED THEIR CRAZY,' SAYS IT COULD SPELL TROUBLE IN 2028 "But again, as I said at the beginning, it's like you expect me to bow down to just one side of it, the left side of it. I'm the bad person because I'm questioning things," Maher said during the discussion with Bateman. "We're going to abolish the police, that everything is going to be free. I mean, their website literally says, 'Imagine this world where you don't have to worry about rent. You don't have to worry about transportation." He continued, "But you're the good people. You're the smart people. You're the people who shouldn't be questioned." The DSA did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. SOCIALISTS LAUNCH RADICAL PLATFORM TO ABOLISH THE US SENATE IN BID TO FUNDAMENTALLY TRANSFORM AMERICA. The DSA's policies drew scrutiny earlier this year after DSA co-chair Megan Romer discussed the organization's positions during an interview in July. Those positions included proposals to abolishing the Senate, police, and prisons. Romer affirmed the organization's support for replacing the presidency and Supreme Court, abolishing ICE, eventually eliminating national borders while granting amnesty to people living in the country illegally, defunding the Pentagon, phasing out prisons and shifting most large corporations to public ownership during the interview. BILL MAHER ADMITS HE COULD VOTE FOR JD VANCE, WARNS 'COWARDLY' DEMOCRATS FACE SOCIALIST TAKEOVER "This is not about politics. This is about – and I was saying to the guys earlier, like to me, being an American is, I am free to pursue the kind of life I want and to do whatever I want so long as what I'm doing doesn't impinge on somebody else's ability to do the same. Now, the stuff they're talking about impinges on my ability. And this is not conducive to an American society," Bateman said. Maher said he agreed and noted that he had told Vice President JD Vance in June that his vote was in play for Republicans if Democrats continued down this path. "That's why I told the vice president, 'My vote is in play.' And then, of course, within 24 hours they wrote, 'Bill Maher is a Republican now.' I never said that. I'm not. I said my vote is in play," Maher said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Author, psychotherapist and cultural commentator Jonathan Alpert told Fox News Digital, "Here's a guy who's been a liberal his entire life, and now he's talking about voting Republican. That should tell Democrats something. He's not the one who's changed his politics dramatically. He's questioning how far some people on the left want to go." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Bateman makes a good point," Alpert added. "What exactly happens if you get rid of police and prisons? Are we supposed to naively believe violent criminals will suddenly behave themselves? It's absurd to think you can just get rid of the institutions you don't like and somehow everything will work out. Human nature doesn't change because you pass a law. Maher and Bateman aren't asking anything outrageous. They're simply asking people to think through the consequences of what they're proposing. If you want to abolish prisons and police, you should be able to explain how you're going to keep people safe. That's not an unreasonable expectation."

articles.title: Denmark, Estonia express skepticism over Finland and Norway’s call with Putin
articles.summary: Danish and Estonian officials expressed skepticism over leadership from Finland and Norway communicating with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier this week amid heightened tension between Moscow and Kyiv. Estonian Foreign Affairs Minister Margus Tsahkna wrote on social platform X, “Only increased pressure on Russia will make it take peace negotiations seriously.” “Every contact with Russia…
articles.body:
Danish and Estonian officials expressed skepticism over leadership from Finland and Norway communicating with Russian President Vladimir Putin earlier this week amid heightened tension between Moscow and Kyiv.

Estonian Foreign Affairs Minister Margus Tsahkna wrote on social platform X , “Only increased pressure on Russia will make it take peace negotiations seriously.”

“Every contact with Russia must convey Europe’s unity and determination to support Ukraine and maintain pressure on Russia, while making clear that Europe will not negotiate away the fundamental principles underpinning its security,” Tsahkna continued, adding that “there is no indication that Russia has changed its strategic objectives or is genuinely interested in negotiations.”

“A just and lasting peace requires increased pressure on Russia, tighter sanctions, action against sanctions evasion, Russia’s international isolation and unwavering support for Ukraine,” he stated.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb’s office confirmed the call between the trio on Tuesday, writing that it was “held in consultation with Ukraine.”

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen reportedly said she was “very skeptical of this Norwegian and Finnish initiative,” according to Bloomberg . She noted that the initiative was “not coordinated with the rest of us.”

Frederiksen added she believed “Russia does not want” peace with Europe “therefore I think we should be very careful about giving Putin an opportunity,” per a translation by Visegrad 24 .

A press release about the call affirmed that while Finland and Norway border Russia, both countries are “firm supporters of Ukraine” and the “aim of the call was to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations to help to end the war.”

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre detailed in the press release that he and Stubb “stressed the importance of de-escalation” to leaders in Russia.

“The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions,” Stubb concluded.

The call marked their first known direct contact since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Upcoming trilateral talks concerning the Ukraine-Russia war are scheduled for later this year in Abu Dhabi, per the Finnish President’s office.

Overnight, Russian ballistic missiles hit multiple targets in Kyiv and Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-largest city, killing at least 3 people, per the Associated Press . Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media that Russia launched 16 missiles and more than 280 drones directed at 11 regions in Ukraine.

articles.title: Harry Kane's first football club celebrates Ballon d'Or win
articles.summary: Ridgeway Rovers FC says it is proud to have produced a Ballon d'Or player in England's Harry Kane.
articles.body:
The chairman of the football club that Harry Kane played for as a boy has said they are proud of his "hard work" after the England captain won the Ballon d'Or.

Ian Marshall, chairman of Ridgeway Rovers FC in Walthamstow, where Kane played as a youth, said he was welling up during the awards, adding: "I know how hard he's worked to get it, and I know what he's had to go through from the beginning."

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker was crowned the world's best male football player and men's striker of the year at the awards on Monday night.

Alex Welsh, former academy coach at Arsenal, said he was "ecstatic" Kane had won the award, which he described as "fully deserved".

"Harry has certainly reached the levels that we could never have foreseen all those years ago," Welsh said.

"The great thing about Harry is he's never forgotten where it all began, here at the Peter May Sports Centre."

The centre is home to Ridgeway Rovers FC and next door to The Arsenal Football Club Youth Academy. It is also home to a Harry Kane statue.

"We want every kid that comes on to this pitch to look at this statue and think, 'That could be me one of these days'," said Welsh.

"If you want to be a professional athlete, look at Harry Kane. What a brilliant role model."

The former academy coach said it was not always certain Kane would make it as a centre forward.

"When Harry was 10, the club weren't quite sure whether he was going to make the cut," he said.

"For my sins I was the part-time goalkeeping coach at the Arsenal Academy and they said, 'Look, he's good in goal, can you take him?'

'So I took him for five months, once a week, and tried to convert him into a goalkeeper.

"But in the end, I failed miserably to convert him into a goalie. The whole nation owes me a debt of gratitude that I was hopeless at my job."

Marshall said Kane's success was due to his continued self-belief and hard work.

"We didn't think he would be as good as he was," he said. "We probably thought he would be a good squad player for a team, but nobody saw what was coming.

"But it's down to him, his effort, his hard work, his application.

"He's better than all the rest of them and that's a fact."

Marshall said the club was considering paying tribute to Kane's Ballon d'Or on their kit.

"We're very proud of that fact," he said. "We're a club that produced a Ballon d'Or player... there's not many of them about."

Stanley, who plays centre midfield for the Ridgeway Rovers Under 10s Tigers, said he wanted to follow Kane's success.

"It's an inspiration for the whole team to follow on his journey," he said.

"[England] are really lucky because without Harry Kane they would be nowhere."

George, who plays centre back, left-mid and right-mid, said he hoped to become a professional football player and reach Kane's standard.

"I was actually sleeping when he won the Ballon d'Or, but when I first heard I was like, 'Get in there'," he said.

"It makes me believe that I can do it and all my other friends can do it as well."

articles.title: Manhunt under way for Tennessee killer Jacob Morley who escaped prison through a fence
articles.summary: Morley was given a life sentence for the 2022 killing of his co-worker Cody Birchfield.
articles.body:
A manhunt is under way in Tennessee after a convicted murderer serving a life sentence escaped from prison.

Jacob Allen Morley, 28, was found guilty of the 2022 killing of his co-worker and sentenced in 2025, prison records show.

He escaped on Sunday from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville, about 90 miles (145 km) north of Memphis, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction (TDOC).

It said security camera footage confirmed Morley had breached the prison's perimeter fence and escaped in his prison uniform.

Investigators have released security camera video they say shows him stealing a nearby farm's work car.

Morley has been added to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation's most wanted list, the TDOC said, and a reward of up to $2,500 (£1,900) is being offered for information leading to his arrest.

Prison staff confirmed he was "unaccounted for" on Sunday night and begun an emergency headcount and search within the prison, officials said on Monday.

"The Tennessee Highway Patrol has deployed aviation assets and state troopers to assist with the search," the TDOC said.

Prison records show his supervision level was listed as "low" and he was not eligible for release until December 2083.

On Tuesday afternoon, investigators said the stolen vehicle had been found in Illinois about 120 miles north of Tiptonville, but Morley was not there.

He was sentenced in June 2025 after being convicted of first-degree murder over the death of his colleague Cody Birchfield in 2022. Birchfield's body was found in a metal box under Morley's home, according to Carter County court records reviewed by the BBC.

Birchfield died "as a result of a gunshot wound to the back of the head", a pathology report cited in court said. Bullet casings matched a gun found in Morley's house.

The pair had developed a friendship while Birchfield was training Morley at the pallet manufacturing company they worked at, Birchfield's sister said in her victim impact statement to the court.

Besides murder, Morley was also convicted of vandalism, tampering with evidence, aggravated burglary, and evading arrest. His request for a new trial was denied in May.

This is not the first time Morley has led law enforcement officials on a manhunt. His 2022 arrest came after a police chase that crossed state lines into North Carolina.

Earlier this month, another prisoner Gregory Redden, 69, who is serving a 15-year sentence for aggravated robbery, escaped from custody but was recaptured shortly after.

Convicted murder Christa Pike survived a botched lethal injection in the state in September, leading to the resignation of TDOC Commissioner Frank Strada.

articles.title: King Charles heads to Caribbean as calls grow for slavery apology
articles.summary: Britain’s King Charles III will begin a tour of the Caribbean on Tuesday as pressure mounts on Britain to apologize and pay reparations for its role in the slave trade.
articles.body: Britain’s King Charles III will begin a tour of the Caribbean on Tuesday as pressure mounts on Britain to apologize and pay reparations for its role in the slave trade. Charles will arrive in the Bahamas at the start of a nine-day visit that will also take in Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda, where he and Queen Camilla will attend the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM), a biennial summit of 56 nations. Charles’s first visit to the Caribbean as monarch comes amid growing calls for Britain to make reparations for its leading role in the transatlantic slave trade. Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey said last week it was time for discussions about reparations. Asked by Sky News whether the King should apologize over Britain’s historic role in the slave trade, Botchwey said: “It wouldn’t hurt to have that.” “That’s what the countries have asked for,” Botchwey added. “I don’t believe we can run away from it. But it is important to determine the form that reparations should take, and that is something that will emerge eventually.” Meanwhile, the Caribbean Community, or Caricom, a group of 23 member and associate member states, said last month it would push for reparations to be on the agenda at CHOGM. “The Caribbean has consistently asserted that reparations is fundamentally about justice,” Caricom Secretary-General Carla Barnett said in a speech. “It is about recognition, accountability and transformation, and about building a just and equitable future for the descendants of those who, as the chattel of colonial owners, endured untold suffering, loss of life and freedom.” The king can only act on the advice of his ministers when he represents the country abroad, and despite the renewed calls, he has continued to follow the British government advice against issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in the slave trade. Buckingham Palace has said he will not apologize during the Caribbean tour as such questions were “matters for governments to address,” but that he will “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.” At the last CHOGM, in 2024, Charles acknowledged that “the most painful aspects of our past continue to resonate.” However, he stopped short of an official apology and did not directly engage on the subject. Jonathan Reynolds, the United Kingdom’s business secretary, said Tuesday that reparations are not a “reasonable request.” Reynolds told Sky News that he was “sensitive to British history” and that “we should be able to talk about it” but that past events should not be attributed to current generations. In recent years, the British monarchy has adopted a more conciliatory tone when addressing the horrors of slavery. During a visit to Kenya in 2023, his first trip to a Commonwealth nation as head of the body, Charles said the “wrongdoings of the past are a cause of the greatest sorrow and the deepest regret.” At least 12.5 million Africans were abducted and sold into slavery by European merchants between the 15th and 19th centuries, and Britain is estimated to have had a role in transporting about 3.2 million people. When slavery was abolished in Britain in 1834, the government compensated slave owners the equivalent of £17 billion ($22.5 billion), but slaves received nothing, according to research by University College London.

articles.title: Israeli voter turnout hits 53-year high as Netanyahu fights to stay in power
articles.summary: Voter turnout in Israel’s election on Tuesday hit a 53-year high as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, already the longest-serving leader in the country’s history, fights to hold on to power as he faces opposition over his handling of the wars in Gaza and Iran. Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout was at 55.7 percent…
articles.body:
Voter turnout in Israel’s election on Tuesday hit a 53-year high as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, already the longest-serving leader in the country’s history, fights to hold on to power as he faces opposition over his handling of the wars in Gaza and Iran.

Israel’s Central Elections Committee said voter turnout was at 55.7 percent at 4 p.m. (10 a.m. EST), having reached 47.5 percent by that time during the 2022 election.

“There hasn’t been such a nationwide voter turnout since 1973,” Acting director general of the Central Elections Committee Dean Livne told The Times of Israel , later saying that more than 4 million people have cast their ballots.

Livne said the city with the highest turnout so far was Modiin, at 60.7 percent, followed by Tel Aviv at 50.5 percent and Jerusalem at 47.7 percent.

Ofer Kenig, a research fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute told CNN that based on the early results, election officials have seen an increase “in all sectors” except in the “ultra-orthodox cities, [where] we see a decrease in voter turnout.”

“In other segments of the Israeli society, we see an increase,” Kenig said. “Very, very cautiously we can see a higher increase in liberal strongholds rather than the Netanyahu coalition strongholds.”

Kenig noted that some groups may choose to go vote later in the day. Polls close at 10 p.m. local time, likely leading to a tight outcome between Netanyahu and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader.

Eisenkot, while casting his ballot in Herzliya, urged “all Israelis to go vote and stick to the mission of replacing the worst government since the state’s founding,” CNN reported.

“I suggest not to get excited by Netanyahu’s scare tactics,” he said outside the polling station, according to the outlet.

Netanyahu cast his ballot at a polling station in Jerusalem, calling Tuesday’s election a “very moving and fateful moment.”

The prime minister’s political future hangs in the balance amid growing frustration over his handling of the Iran war and response to the Hamas-led terror attack on Oct. 7, 2023, which he was reportedly warned about in the days before the attack. The International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for Netanyahu in 2024, accusing the prime minister of war crimes for his military campaign in the Gaza Strip.

Netanyahu has also faced accusations of corruption amid a years-long bribery case that has gone to trial, one in which his request for a presidential pardon was denied.

The prime minister has denied any wrongdoing in connection with the corruption trial and the war crime accusations, and has defended Israel’s actions in Gaza as having “prevented genocide.”

Netanyahu received President Trump’s endorsement , who praised the prime minister’s leadership during the eight-month-long Iran war.

“Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself,” Trump wrote on Truth Social last week. “Despite all of that, he has endured and, in fact, he has thrived!”

articles.title: White House defends Trump after archbishop apologises over ‘manipulated’ prayer moment ahead of midterms
articles.summary: The White House has defended US President Donald Trump after Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob apologised for participating in an Oval Office prayer with
articles.body: The White House has defended US President Donald Trump after Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob apologised for participating in an Oval Office prayer with the president, accusing the administration of turning the religious gathering into a political photo opportunity less than two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.Grob, in a statement titled “A Public Apology” published on the Archdiocese of Milwaukee’s website on Sunday, said the White House had distributed photographs and video of the October 22 meeting without the consent of the 12 participating bishops. He accused the administration of manipulating a sacred moment for partisan political purposes.The archbishop said he had received messages from Catholics concerned that his participation could be interpreted as an endorsement of Trump or his administration. He expressed regret over the distress caused by his involvement, adding that he had reservations about attending the meeting but wished he had given them greater consideration.“I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way,” Grob said.“We came in good faith to try to work for the betterment of our fellow human beings, to ease their suffering, to build up the common good, and to pray with a president, not to pose for a political photo opportunity to benefit the few,” he added.White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers defended Trump’s record on religious freedom and issues important to Catholic Americans in a statement to Fox News Digital following Grob’s apology.“There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it,” Rogers said, citing the administration’s actions on religious liberty, pardons for anti-abortion activists and parental rights.The meeting, organised by the conservative Heritage Foundation, was intended to discuss issues including immigration enforcement, religious worker visas and human dignity, according to Grob.After a discussion with White House officials and advisers, the bishops entered the Oval Office, where Trump presented commemorative tokens before praying with them. Grob said the bishops had been informed that there would be an opportunity to pray with the president, but were unaware that a video was being recorded and had not given permission for the footage or photographs to be publicly distributed.Des Moines Bishop William Joensen, another participant, also criticised the political implications of the gathering in a statement published on Saturday. He said the bishops had been aware that the meeting took place close to a national election but had not intended to endorse any candidate or political party.“In no way did any of us intend by our involvement to endorse any political party or any individual candidate,” Joensen said, adding that the gathering had been exploited for partisan purposes.Denver Archbishop James Golka, who led the prayer, also addressed the controversy in an interview with the Denver Catholic. He acknowledged concerns that the footage could be used politically but defended the decision to pray with Trump, saying Catholics traditionally pray for elected officials regardless of political disagreements.“I wasn’t sure what to do. On one hand, it was a great opportunity to raise important issues for the Church’s benefit,” Golka said, adding that he had recognised the possibility that the meeting could be shared publicly and used for political purposes.“But as I prayed about it, I thought that this is what Catholics do,” he said. “We pray for people. No matter whether we agree or disagree on anything, we always pray for our country and leaders.”The controversy comes amid disagreements between Catholic leaders and the Trump administration over immigration policy. The US Conference of Catholic Bishops sued the administration in February 2025 over the suspension of refugee resettlement funding.Grob had also joined other Wisconsin bishops earlier this year in issuing a statement criticising the administration’s treatment of immigrants.Other Catholic leaders have urged continued engagement with the administration despite policy differences. Bishop Robert Barron, a member of Trump’s Religious Liberty Commission, cautioned against demonising the president in a May interview with Fox News Digital.“What I don’t want from the church is a kind of demonization of the Trump administration,” Barron said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russell Brand told police he never had non-consensual sex
articles.summary: His trial hears statements he gave to police between 2023 and 2025, denying allegations against him.
articles.body:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

Russell Brand told police in interviews in response to allegations of rape and sexual assault that he had been "very promiscuous" in the past, but had never engaged in "non-consensual sexual activity", a court has heard.

Brand, 51, was interviewed four times between 2023 and 2025 by officers.

The TV and media personality is currently on trial at Southwark Crown Court in London on three counts of rape and other offences. He denies all the charges.

Jurors heard on Tuesday that he gave a prepared statement in each of the police interviews. In November 2023, he said: "I have repeatedly stated publicly and written extensively that I led a very promiscuous life, that I have spent years openly denouncing. I have never engaged in non-consensual activity."

Brand went on to say the allegations were made in "a defamatory and fictitious documentary", which he said contained "false and anonymised" interviews.

He added that "subsequently both the media and the police publicly invited additional allegations to be made, which has resulted in further encounters to be invented or reimagined".

In court on Tuesday, the jury was also asked formally to find Brand not guilty of a charge of indecent assault.

The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, said there was "insufficient evidence to support the charge of indecent assault".

This charge related to a woman who said Brand grabbed her arm and tried to drag her into a toilet in 2001 when she worked at MTV.

The jury was then given an amended indictment, which charges Brand with attempted indecent assault. Brand has pleaded not guilty to this charge.

The prosecution will conclude on Wednesday morning before the defence is expected to start.

Brand denies three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault.

articles.title: Plan for bigger, heavier, stealthy next-generation destroyers gets defence council’s approval
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The long-pending next-generation destroyer programme has received a formal push with the Rajnath Singh-led Defence Acquisition Council (DAC)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The long-pending next-generation destroyer programme has received a formal push with the Rajnath Singh-led Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) giving its in-principle approval to the futuristic warships under Project 18A on Monday under the “naval platforms” category.The proposed stealth guided-missile destroyers, to be designed by Warship Design Bureau, will be bigger, heavier and equipped with advanced weapons and technologies and part of future frontline surface combatants of the Indian Navy. The project may cost upwards of Rs 75,000 crore and the delivery is likely to start 5-10 years after the contract is signed. “The futuristic destroyers will have displacement upwards of 10,000 tonnes, making them significantly larger than the Visakhapatnam-class destroyers (7,400 tonnes),” a source told TOI. “These warships will have more firepower, more sensors, advanced technologies and systems,” the source said. A competitive bidding will happen in the near future for the building of these next-generation destroyers.Indian Navy currently operates around 12-13 relatively new guided-missile destroyers that serve as the backbone of its surface combat fleet, providing multi-domain capabilities in air defence, anti-surface warfare, and anti-submarine operations. There are four destroyers — INS Visakhapatnam, INS Mormugao, INS Imphal, INS Surat — under Visakhapatnam-Class (Project 15B); three destroyers like INS Kolkata, INS Kochi, INS Chennai under Kolkata-Class (Project 15A); three destroyers (INS Delhi, INS Mysore, INS Mumbai) under Delhi-Class (Project 15); and some Soviet-built destroyers (Rajput-Class (Kashin-II/Project 61-ME) that are being phased out.An active Indian Navy destroyer is currently equipped with a comprehensive suite of anti-surface, anti-air, and anti-submarine weapons: each has around 16 BrahMos cruise missiles; 32 medium-to-long-range surface-to-air missiles stored in vertical launching systems; one 76 mm OTO Melara naval gun mounted forward of the bridge; four AK-630 30 mm Gatling guns for point defence against incoming missiles and aircraft, twin 21-inch torpedo tubes capable of firing heavy-weight torpedoes and two RBU-6000 anti-submarine rocket launchers. The futuristic destroyers will have much more than these lethal weapons.As per the defence ministry’s Monday statement, 82% of the overall DAC-cleared defence proposals are earmarked for the domestic defence industry under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat framework. So, the futuristic destroyers are likely to have more indigenous content, thus reducing dependence on imports.

articles.title: Newsom signs order protecting Pacific Coast Highway from El Niño’s powerful storms
articles.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order Tuesday to protect the iconic Pacific Coast Highway from the impacts of El Niño-related storms.
articles.body: California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed an executive order Tuesday to protect the iconic Pacific Coast Highway from the impacts of El Niño-related storms as a potentially stormy winter approaches. This action comes on the heels of the Democratic governor’s state of emergency declaration issued on Sept. 21, which freed up resources to prepare for what is predicted to be the strongest El Niño event on record to affect California. El Niño is a naturally occurring climate cycle characterized by hotter than normal ocean temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean and altered winds and precipitation patterns along the equator. El Niño has ripple effects on weather patterns worldwide, contributing to a variety of extreme weather events. It can cause flooding in some regions and drought in others. While an intense El Niño does not necessarily mean related extreme weather events will be stronger, it does increase the odds that these extremes will occur. One of the hallmarks of El Nino is its potential to send powerful, moisture-laden storms into the Golden State that bring high winds, towering waves and heavy rainfall, all of which threaten the stability of coastal transportation corridors like Highway 1. High waves have already caused erosion to eat away at the scenic highway. El Niño-driven high tides and pounding surf can significantly worsen such erosion to the point where some coastal roads and rail lines are no longer safe to travel on. The order creates a Highway 1 task force, led by the state transportation and natural resources agencies, to prepare the roadway for coastal storms and tackle longer-term climate change risks. “Highway 1 is more than our nation’s most iconic roadway. It keeps our coastal economy moving,” Newsom said in a statement. “It gets people to work, children to school, goods to local businesses, first responders where they’re needed, and visitors to our legendary beaches.” “We know what repeated closures cost these communities, and we’re putting state agencies to work now to reduce the danger before storms hit,” Newsom said. Newsom also signed another executive order that builds upon the September emergency proclamation, to help communities prepare for storms before they arrive. The order gives state agencies additional tools to reduce flood risks and protect critical infrastructure from the potential impacts of El Niño.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro's passports cancelled after he fails to surrender them
articles.summary: The defeated presidential candidate is under investigation for alleged money laundering and barred from leaving Brazil.
articles.body:
Police in Brazil say they have cancelled the passports of the defeated right-wing presidential candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, after he failed to comply with an order to surrender the documents.

On Monday, the Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to hand his passports over to police within 24 hours as part of an investigation into alleged money laundering, which he denies.

At the time, Bolsonaro said he had no plans to leave the country, and insisted that he would stay in Brazil to lead the opposition to his left-wing rival, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

However, the deadline has passed without the senator surrendering the passports, prompting speculation he may have left the country.

Bolsonaro's lawyers told BBC Brasil that they were "completely in the dark" about his whereabouts.

"We knew nothing about this, and we still have no information about what happened," one lawyer said.

Bolsonaro has not made any public statements since Monday afternoon local time, when he posted a video on social media.

Federal officers are checking border crossings to establish if Bolsonaro may have travelled to neighbouring Argentina, according to a police source consulted by BBC News Brasil.

However, Argentine authorities have told the BBC there is no record of Bolsonaro entering their country through any border crossing.

Bolsonaro was already under investigation for alleged corruption over the financing of a film about his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who was convicted of plotting a coup and is under house arrest.

In addition to that investigation, Brazil's Supreme Court ordered police on Tuesday to probe Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral campaign over alleged foreign funding.

The 45-year-old senator suffered a stinging defeat on Sunday when he was beaten by Lula in a presidential run-off, which Bolsonaro had been widely expected to win.

His younger brother Eduardo Bolsonaro lives in the Texas, in the US, but was in Miami on Sunday, where he cast his vote at a polling station and attended an election viewing event which was streamed to his followers.

Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback

Opinion polls had put him narrowly ahead of Lula and analysts pointed out that Bolsonaro's win in the first round of the election on 4 October, meant he was likely to take victory in the run-off.

But after an early lead in the count, he was overtaken by the veteran incumbent, who became the first presidential candidate to overturn a first round loss to win in the second round.

Lula won 51.79% of the vote, compared to Bolsonaro's 48.21%.

Despite trailing by 4.4 million votes, Bolsonaro has not conceded and has called for the election to be annulled.

He argues that he was put at a disadvantage because polling was extended by two hours on election day - even though the extension was requested by both his party and that of his rival.

He called the extension, which was ordered by a Supreme Court justice, a "dirty trick".

However the party he represented, the Liberal Party, has accepted the result, although it did say that the extension of voting "merits investigation".

articles.title: Spain deports migrants from Ceuta in move criticised by rights group
articles.summary: The deportation was the first of its kind since a mass border crossing into the territory from Morocco in July.
articles.body:
Spain has deported more than a dozen migrants from its North African enclave of Ceuta, prompting criticism from Amnesty International, which said Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s left-wing government was endangering their human rights.

It was the first deportation of its kind since a mass border crossing into the territory from Morocco in July.

The Spanish Interior Ministry said on Tuesday that it had deported the migrants from Ceuta after their asylum applications were rejected, and that Morocco had agreed to receive them.

Nongovernmental organisations (NGOs) told the Reuters news agency that 16 people from African, Middle Eastern and Asian countries had been deported.

About 80,000 people entered from Morocco over a 48-hour period in late July. At least 100 people died during the mass crossing into the autonomous city, which covers just 18.5 square kilometres (7.2sq miles) and has a population of about 80,000.

The crisis has evolved into a major political challenge for Sanchez, who is seeking re-election in snap polls scheduled for November 29.

Tens of thousands of protesters have gathered across Spain in recent months to denounce the government’s handling of the situation. Meanwhile, right-wing parties have used the crisis to attack Sanchez.

The leader of the far-right Vox Party, Santiago Abascal, has branded the prime minister a “traitor”.

Amnesty International has warned that the human rights of those deported from Ceuta on Tuesday could be at risk.

“Spain, despite its [progressive] speeches in Europe, is not ensuring that human rights guarantees are met for people who cross its borders in Ceuta and Melilla,” said Virginia Alvarez, an Amnesty International researcher.

“Morocco does not respect many human rights.”

However, Madrid disputes the rights group’s accusations. In a statement, the interior ministry told Reuters that the European Union considers Morocco to be a safe country, adding that deportations are carried out “with all the necessary safeguards”.

Most of those who entered Ceuta in late July left within days. However, about 8,000 migrants still remain. Some are sleeping on the streets, while others are being housed by Spain, charities and civil society groups.
