articles.title: Trump says he will ban the term 'artificial intelligence', wants it called 'super intelligence'
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said his administration would ban the term “artificial intelligence” in official documents, calling it inaccurate.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said his administration would ban the term “artificial intelligence” in official documents, calling it inaccurate. He said the technology should instead be called “super intelligence”.In a post on Truth Social, Trump questioned why The Wall Street Journal was not using his preferred term, “SI”, short for super intelligence."When will The Wall Street Journal start calling Artificial Intelligence (AI), a very bad and inaccurate name, SI (Super Intelligence), the name which virtually everyone else is using, or soon will be," Trump said."In short order, we will be officially banning the term, “AI/Artificial Intelligence,” in all relevant documents, and everything else, due to its inaccuracy."Trump's remarks came following an executive order he signed on September 30, titled “Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence”.The order directs federal departments and agencies to replace the terms “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official communications and operations, to the extent permitted by law.The revised terminology is to be used in government correspondence, public communications, official websites, reports and administrative policy documents. However, existing regulations, government contracts, grants and historical archival records will not be changed retroactively.Explaining the rationale, the order said advances in technology had outgrown the original framework used to describe artificial intelligence.“The capabilities of today’s frontier systems do much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence. They increasingly amplify human ingenuity and unlock new forms of creativity, empowering Americans to achieve what was previously impossible across science, medicine, and nearly every other domain of human endeavor,” the order stated, news agency ANI reported.The directive also gives the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology 60 days to submit proposed legislation to Congress defining “Super Intelligence” under federal law and recommending corresponding changes to existing laws.The move follows a White House meeting between Trump and leading technology executives, including Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Sundar Pichai and Jensen Huang, to discuss technological advances and the safe development of advanced systems.Trump described the sector’s growth as unprecedented, while industry leaders stressed the importance of collaboration and safety.The proposed change marks a shift in the terminology the Trump administration wants federal agencies to use when referring to advanced technologies.You use AI every day. articles.title: Defeated candidate Flávio Bolsonaro defies Brazil travel ban with flight to US, sources say
articles.summary: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil and is headed to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election, two sources have confirmed to CNN.
articles.body: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil and is headed to the United States after losing Sunday’s presidential election, two sources have confirmed to CNN. A US official initially told CNN that Bolsonaro was headed to Florida, but later said his exact destination in the US was unclear. A Brazilian source close to Bolsonaro said that the politician had feared arrest in Brazil. He is currently under investigation by the country’s highest court for alleged acts of corruption, money laundering and currency evasion. Speculation about his movements mounted after Argentine news outlet Infobae reported that Bolsonaro had left Brazil via Argentina after losing Sunday’s runoff presidential election against leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The Argentine government said in a statement that it has “no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering” the country. Brazil’s Federal Police canceled Bolsonaro’s passports after he failed to surrender them and are currently searching for him, affiliate CNN Brasil reported. Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro to turn in his passports within 24 hours on Monday. CNN has reached out to Bolsonaro, his political party and the Brazilian Federal Police for comment on the senator’s whereabouts. Bolsonaro said Brazilian police had informed him of the order in person and told him he was banned from leaving Brazil. In a video posted to Instagram, the senator denied that he intended to flee. One of the allegations against Bolsonaro is connected to potential illegal online betting platforms, and another to the production of a biopic about his father, “Dark Horse,” which federal police believe involved funds from Banco Master, a now-collapsed bank at the heart of a $7 billion Ponzi-like scheme in 2025. Bolsonaro denies all wrongdoing. At the time of his departure from Brazil, there were no warrants for his arrest, but according to legal analysts, the act of defying the court’s orders to surrender his passports could be enough reason for a warrant to be issued. Right-wingers in exile In leaving Brazil for the US, Bolsonaro joins a large community of Brazilian conservatives in exile – including his own brother Eduardo, former Brazilian intelligence chief Alexandre Ramagem and podcaster Paulo Figueiredo. Eduardo suggested shortly before the runoff election that Flávio ought to leave Brazil if his bid for the presidency failed. On Tuesday, Eduardo called rumors that his brother had fled a “lie.” Flávio’s journey mirrors his father’s actions after losing the 2022 presidential election. Shortly after his loss, Jair Bolsonaro decamped for Orlando, Florida, where he remained for three months. During that time, hundreds of his supporters stormed the seats of power in the capital Brasília, vandalizing the supreme court, congress and the presidential palace in an attack reminiscent of the insurrection on the US Capitol in 2021. Bolsonaro and his allies’ efforts to overturn the 2022 election results led to the former president being sentenced to 27 years in prison. US President Donald Trump, a prominent supporter of the Bolsonaro family, briefly imposed tariffs on Brazil in response to the criminal case against Jair. Trump claimed without evidence earlier this week that Lula’s victory was “rigged.” Bolsonaro’s leaving Brazil comes directly after his surprise loss to Lula over the weekend. The conservative politician was a strong favorite to win, but Lula managed to outmaneuver Bolsonaro Sunday, earning 4.4 million more votes in the second round. Bolsonaro initially refused to concede to Lula, saying his team would ask for the results to be annulled. Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party reversed course days later. “We recognize the presidential election results,” party head Valdemar Costa Neto said, according to CNN Brasil. “But we believe the issues ⁠raised need to be properly clarified.”

articles.body: 25-year-old Katherine Kelly, a Florida woman, tracked down her boyfriend after suspecting that he was with another woman and then shot at the other woman who was sitting inside a car. articles.body: PARK CITY, Utah — Authorities in Utah are holding a news conference Tuesday to pin another decades-old homicide on serial killer Ted Bundy. The Summit County sheriff and county attorney “will provide information regarding the investigation, the findings that led to this conclusion, and the decision to close the case,” the sheriff’s office said. The victim's name has not been released yet, though the local death of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith in 1974 has long been listed as a cold case. Bundy has been dead for nearly 40 years, but the tally of his confirmed victims continues to grow due to advances in DNA testing. Bundy killed at least 30 women and girls in multiple states in the 1970s, and many more escaped or survived with injuries. In April, Utah authorities said Bundy was responsible for the murder of Laura Ann Aime, 17, who disappeared on Halloween in 1974. He was executed in 1989 by electric chair in Florida for the 1978 murders of two women at the Chi Omega sorority house at Florida State University. Bundy gave a series of confessions in his final days, including to some crimes that were previously unknown to police. Not all of those cases have been confirmed.

articles.title: Chancellor John Healey's Budget to include £15m to tackle misogyny
articles.summary: The Conservatives doubt whether women and girls will feel safer as a result of the funding.
articles.body:
Chancellor John Healey has pledged to give £15m to a fund established to tackle misogyny in schools, at work and in communities.

The government said the money will be provided over three years to schemes such as mentoring for young people, workplace training and communications campaigns designed to improve women and girls' safety.

Speaking on the eve of his first Budget, Healey said: "Every woman and girl deserves to feel safe, respected and able to pursue their ambitions - at school, at work and in their communities."

But Conservative shadow women and equalities minister Joy Morrissey said "not a single woman and girl is going to feel safer with this total waste of public money".

Swinney to introduce misogyny education in every school in Scotland

Women to advise mayor how to make London safer

Students face sexism and misogyny at weekend jobs

The "misogyny prevention fund" is expected to be confirmed in the Budget and is intended to support the work of a national taskforce established last month and chaired by Women and Equalities Minister Bridget Phillipson.

Healey said the money will support "practical action to tackle misogyny head-on" and he hopes it will attract additional funding from businesses and philanthropists to increase its reach.

Phillipson said daily incidents of misogyny, including sexist slurs and workplace discrimination, have "no place in modern Britain".

She said: "This funding is a critical step as we work to confine misogyny to the history books, where it belongs."

Phillipson added that "everyone, from big business to members of the public, can do their bit to stamp out misogyny and improve the lives of women and girls everywhere".

When launching the taskforce chaired by Phillipson, the government said last month that it would aim to ensure government policy is "shaped by those most affected by misogyny".

It added its first meeting would focus on young people and later look at "workplaces, digital spaces and social cohesion".

Statistics published by the Office for National Statistics this month showed an estimated 12.8% of females aged 16 and over in England and Wales - around 3.2m - experienced at least one of domestic abuse, sexual victimisation or stalking in the year to March 2026.

The figure was an estimated 8.9% for males - around 2.1m.

For the Conservatives, Morrissey cited the estimates for women and girls as she criticised the announcement.

She said: "Labour simply aren't serious about tackling the crisis of violence against women and girls.

"This week it seems they will get the hard-pressed British taxpayer to fork out £15m to fund projects to tackle the 'manosphere'."

articles.title: ‘If they’re honest’: Trump casts latest suspicion on US midterm elections
articles.summary: Trump’s comments come as his administration files legal challenges to Democrat-led US states over election integrity.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump said he would respect the results of next week’s midterm elections if they were “honest,” as his administration expanded a legal battle to assert power over state authorities running the highly-watched contest on November 3.

“I will if they’re honest elections,” Trump responded to reporters on Tuesday when asked if he will respect the outcome even if his Republican Party loses control of the US Congress.

Trump’s remarks came a day after his Department of Justice (DOJ) threatened the northwestern state of Washington with legal action if it did not remove around 400 people it claims are not US citizens from its voter registration rolls.

“The timing of this request—one week before the General Election—is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results,” Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs said in a statement on Monday, addressing the request received in a letter that gave the state until Wednesday at noon local time to respond, or face what the DOJ called “emergency relief”.

Hobbs’s office said it was reviewing the list of 400 alleged noncitizens, but had already found some of them to be based on outdated information. The DOJ was citing a record from 1994, for instance, to claim one person was a noncitizen on its list, Hobbs said.

“Washington elections are secure. Cases of voter fraud, including noncitizen voting, are incredibly rare, and every voter attests to their eligibility by signing the declaration on their ballot return envelope in every election,” Hobbs said in the statement.

Last month, the state of Washington successfully argued in a lawsuit that it was not obligated to turn over its entire voter list to the DOJ. It was among dozens of Democrat-led states to have faced the demand from the Trump administration and had courts side with it.

Despite the setbacks in court, Trump’s DOJ has continued to try and cast suspicion on the outcome of the November 3 elections, in particular by attempting to claim large numbers of noncitizens are voting in Democratic-led states, a claim that has been repeatedly dismissed by bipartisan voting rights groups.

Last week, the DOJ filed a lawsuit against the state of Alaska, saying it would seek to block certification of its Senate election if the Republican incumbent, Dan Sullivan, did not win. The DOJ said because the state was allowing another candidate who was also named Dan Sullivan to appear on the ballot, local authorities were failing in their responsibility to fairly run the election. On the ballot, Senator Dan Sullivan appears with information indicating that he is the incumbent.

The Senate race is one of several around the country that could go the way of the Democratic Party and see Trump’s Republicans lose control of the legislative body. On Friday, Trump said he personally had told the DOJ to file the lawsuit against Alaska.

Earlier this month, California said it had received a letter from the DOJ saying the state must review a list of around 20,000 noncitizen voters. California authorities said a large percentage of those on the list were in fact people who appeared to have been born in the US, which would automatically make them eligible voters.

The DOJ has also said it is planning to deploy a record number of election observers across the country on November 3 to watch for any irregularities, despite the objection of local officials in several Democratic-led states, including New Jersey and California. Historically, the DOJ has sent observers to watch for issues at places with a record of civil rights violations and obstacles that would keep minorities or disenfranchised groups from the polls on Election Day.

articles.title: The WhatsApp ‘general’ behind Lula’s election comeback in Brazil
articles.summary: Andre Janones built a WhatsApp army of nearly 11 million subscribers. Did it help Lula win?
articles.body:
As Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva celebrated his election victory on Sunday in Sao Paulo, he placed his hand on the head of a man standing beside him and beaming in a green and yellow Brazilian football jersey.

Lula thanked him for his role in the campaign, calling him “our general”.

Andre Janones, a 42-year-old Brazilian congressman who had spent the final weeks of the presidential run-off building a mass online movement to get Lula re-elected, then embraced the president.

“He played an exponential role in this campaign in lifting the morale of our troops every day, morning, noon and night,” Lula told thousands of supporters who packed Paulista Avenue, the city’s main artery.

Just three weeks earlier, the president seemed to be in trouble. He had finished behind his right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro after the first round of voting, his campaign struggling to keep up with the right’s powerful social media operation.

Janones, who had also helped coordinate Lula’s digital operation in his run-off against Jair Bolsonaro in 2022, was convinced Lula’s campaign needed a change – and that he could help turn things around.

He posted a video declaring, “We are going to win this election. Lula will be re-elected president of Brazil.”

His plan centred on a WhatsApp channel he had launched months earlier.

Called Exercito do Lula, or “Lula’s Army”, it had about 60,000 followers after the first round.

By election day, Lula’s Army had grown to almost 11 million subscribers, with Janones widely credited with helping Lula stage his comeback.

How Andre Janones built Lula’s WhatsApp army

Janones is a lawyer and congressman who grew up in a working-class family in Minas Gerais. He made a name for himself through his social media commentary during Brazil’s 2018 truckers’ strike and was elected to Congress that year.

In 2022, he dropped his own presidential bid to endorse Lula, joining his run-off campaign.

“At the time, he became widely known for employing tactics similar to those used by Bolsonarism, despite operating on the left,” said Viktor Chagas, a professor at Fluminense Federal University who studies digital politics and online campaigning.

Janones coined the term “cultural Janonism” to describe his approach, which relied on urgent messages, memes and calls for supporters to take action, as well as what Chagas described as the occasional use of negative campaigning and “content of questionable origin”.

But the scale of Lula’s Army in 2026 was unprecedented, Chagas said.

In the video declaring that Lula would win, Janones urged supporters to enlist as “soldiers” by posting saluting emojis and joining his WhatsApp channel, where he assigned them what he called “missions”.

The tasks were simple, from recruiting three friends to sharing campaign videos to promoting hashtags.

They came in a relentless stream of messages from Janones himself, often written in capital letters. Supporters couldn’t reply, but they could forward the messages or react with emojis, often doing so in the tens of thousands.

Chagas described the strategy as a form of “electoral gamification”, with Janones setting targets for supporters to reach together.

For Andre Pagliarini, an assistant professor of history and international studies at Louisiana State University and the author of a book on Lula, the appeal of Janones’s approach was giving people something they could actually do to help Lula win.

“It became an organising platform that grew exponentially because it spoke to a desire that many Lula supporters evidently had to do something tangible to defeat Flavio Bolsonaro,” he said.

But the path to victory wasn’t just about mobilising supporters online.

Pagliarini credited the campaign for also finding a more effective way to tell the story of the president’s working-class past.

“The campaign’s mistake in the first round was to present this history as a finished monument, worthy of admiration but distant from the lives of the people it was meant to represent,” he wrote.

After Bolsonaro mocked the president for having nine fingers during the final televised debate, for example, Lula responded by recalling how he lost a finger at 17 while working a night shift at a factory. He then linked his experience to workers injured as a result of employers’ negligence.

“Unlike Flavio, he reminded voters, he knew the world of work because he had lived in it,” said Pagliarini.

After the debate, Janones spread the message online, promoting the hashtag #SomosTodos9Dedos, or “We Are All Nine Fingers”. Supporters shared the slogan, with some posting photographs of their own amputated fingers in solidarity.

Janones had also publicly called for simpler, less polished campaign videos that showed a more relatable side of Lula, drinking coffee, visiting people’s homes and talking to ordinary Brazilians. Around the same time, the campaign started posting more informal, selfie-style videos.

“Lula was looser in his political communication, less mediated,” Pagliarini said.

It is difficult to establish whether Janones’s digital army actually delivered votes.

“I am not sure there is a way to empirically connect the group to the outcome,” Pagliarini said.

But he believes Janones helped turn the campaign around.

“Janones himself became a kind of character in the campaign, a cheerleading strategist who seemed confident in a plan that had been missing throughout much of the race,” wrote Pagliarini.

Chagas agreed that it was “difficult to imagine the outcome we achieved without Lula’s Army”, adding that the channel brought together left-wing supporters who had previously been scattered across fragmented online communities, and gave them a way to work together.

The challenge now is keeping that momentum going, Chagas said, pointing to the far right’s use of “permanent campaigning”, maintaining the engagement of supporters between elections.

On election night, at least, Janones kept his soldiers busy.

“EVERYONE TO PAULISTA TO CELEBRATE,” he wrote, urging them to gather on Sao Paulo’s Paulista Avenue. “NOW.”

Later, he asked them not to go to sleep, adding that he’d let them go once he got back from the celebrations.

“Then we’ll discuss a few days off for you,” he joked in a message that drew more than 225,000 reactions.

articles.title: Russia jails IT worker for 13 years for donating money to Ukraine
articles.summary: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance shared Ukraine donation data with Russian authorities resulting in his conviction.
articles.body:
A Russian military court has sentenced an IT specialist to 13 years in prison for financing “terrorism” after the cryptocurrency exchange Binance gave Russian investigators details of his donations to Ukrainian fundraising campaigns.

The 2nd Western District Military Court on Monday convicted 49-year-old Yuri Belenkiy and sentenced him to three years in prison followed by 10 years in a strict-regime penal colony, according to a court statement.

Russian state news agency TASS reported that Belenkiy is a former IT director of the company DiHouse and that prosecutors had asked for 14 years. He was also fined 500,000 roubles ($6,300).

Belenkiy, who holds a Bulgarian residence permit, was detained in September last year when he flew to Moscow for a visit. He denied the charges, and his defence will appeal the verdict, according to TASS.

According to the RIA Novosti news agency, the court found that between August 2022 and March 2024, Belenkiy made 15 cryptocurrency transfers worth more than 120,000 roubles ($1,500) to fund Ukraine’s armed forces and the Azov battalion, which Russia designates a “terrorist” organisation. He used payment details posted by Arkady Babchenko, an exiled Russian journalist and Kremlin critic. RIA added that Belenkiy is on the Russian financial monitoring agency’s list of “terrorists and extremists”.

Russian law enforcement documents seen by the Reuters news agency showed that Binance gave investigators Belenkiy’s transaction history in response to a Russian request. The documents also showed that the records were instrumental in prosecuting him.

“The response from Binance serves as key evidence in the criminal case against Belenkiy,” Yevgeny Smirnov, a lawyer with the rights group First Department, which assists people facing politically motivated prosecutions in Russia, told Reuters.

In court, however, the defence questioned whether the data really came from Binance, noting that the exchange has not cooperated with Russia since 2022, TASS reported.

Asked about the sentence, Binance referred Reuters to a previous statement saying the exchange “does not make or enforce the laws of any jurisdiction, determine charges, or decide how any government uses information in legal proceedings”. It said it does not comment on confidential law enforcement requests or individual cases.

Binance pulled out of the Russian market in 2023, after Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and Western sanctions that followed. Mike Bystrov, a lawyer specialising in crypto regulation, told Reuters in August that the exchange had been under no obligation to provide Belenkiy’s data. Because of Belenkiy’s Bulgarian residency, Bystrov said, Binance may in fact have been obliged under European Union data protection law not to do so.

First Department claimed in a recent report that about 10 percent of all charges brought under the country’s treason and espionage laws in 2025 were linked to donations to Ukrainian organisations. The group said authorities track cryptocurrency transfers as well as bank payments, and continue to open cases over donations made as early as 2022.

articles.title: Deaths in detention cells in Nigeria were entirely preventable, inquiry finds
articles.summary: Overcrowding and poor ventilation caused the deaths of 33 detainees in a prison cell in Minna state.
articles.body:
An inquiry into the deaths of 33 detainees in Nigeria's Minna state has found they died as a result of severe overcrowding, poor ventilation and failure by officers to respond to distress calls.

Forensic and medical evidence showed the "entirely preventable" deaths had resulted from acute respiratory failure linked to prolonged confinement, aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.

The evidence did not support initial claims of a disease outbreak.

The detainees were found dead on 17 September while being held by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps on suspicion of illegal mining. The investigation found that the mining sites had been licensed.

'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria

Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said those found responsible for the deaths would face the full force of the law.

He added that the detention hall had been cleaned before investigators arrived, raising concerns about possible attempts to compromise evidence.

Implicated officers will face suspension and the report would be forwarded to the attorney general of the federation for further legal action, Tunji-Ojo said.

The investigating committee found that the raid on the miners had been conducted without an approved operational order, proper planning or consultation with the Mining Marshals Unit.

It said that 50 detainees had been held in a cell measuring about 20 sq m, with no running water or functioning toilet, and inadequate food, drinking water and airflow.

Adults and minors were detained together, and some detainees were held beyond lawful detention periods.

Officers reportedly ignored repeated calls for help, despite a medical worker having raised concerns about the conditions.

"Detainees repeatedly banged on cell doors and walls, shouted for assistance and pleaded for water," said the head of the investigating team, Jonathan Kure.

"These distress calls were heard by officers assigned to nearby duties... but were not acted upon."

Kure said the detention conditions amounted to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment.

"The tragedy demonstrates the consequences of systemic disregard for detention standards, supervisory responsibilities and the welfare of persons in custody," he added.

The investigating committee also recommended compensation of 30m naira (£16,683; $22,285) for each of the bereaved families and 10m naira for each survivor.

articles.title: Your vacuum cleans your home, but are you cleaning your vacuum? Here’s the right way to do it
articles.summary: To learn how to clean a vacuum, I spoke to a home cleaning expert for their advice and recommendations. Here’s how to do it to make sure your appliance lasts.
articles.body: Your vacuum is probably one of your most used home appliances, particularly if it’s an upright, cordless, robot or handheld model from a popular brand. With that said, it might also be one of the least cleaned appliances in your home. Yes, your vacuum itself should be cleaned from time to time, and this means more than just emptying the dust bin. Depending on what type of vacuum it is, you may have to be more hands on with your cleaning methods. To learn more about how to clean a vacuum without disrupting how well it works, I spoke to a cleaning professional to get their guidance. Below, I rounded up products based on their recommendations and also included popular cleaning tools and appliances that we have tested at NBC Selected. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best products for cleaning a vacuum All of the product recommendations below are based on our previous reporting and/or have at least a four-star average rating from 500 or more customers on Amazon. This brush set includes one long (67-inch) nylon wire hose with wide bristles on one end, and small bristles on the other. It also comes with two short, 8-inch wire brushes with small bristles on the end, which are great for cleaning small holes and tubes. The bendable wires help the brushes clear out debris from tubes that would otherwise be hard to reach, so they’re great for cleaning some parts of vacuums (like the hose or crevice tool), and they’re also ideal for cleaning parts of your fridge or filters for other home appliances. Microfiber cloths are an essential when it comes to any form of cleaning around your home, including cleaning appliances like vacuums. This set includes 12 reusable cloths that are 11.5 by 11.5 inches each, larger than a sheet of copy paper. The cloths are available in more than 10 colors and you can get them in sets of five, eight, 24, 50 and 100. People who bought them say they believe they’re a great value for the price and that they hold up very well, even after months of cleaning and being washed. Ryan Knoll, owner of home cleaning services company Tidy Casa, recommends using Dawn dish soap for cleaning a lot of surfaces around your home, including your vacuum. You can use a small amount of this foaming dish soap spray to coat the dust bin, filter and other parts of your vacuum, and then follow by rinsing and/or wiping cleaning with a microfiber cloth. It’s available in several scents, like apple and lemon, as well as an unscented version (though some versions are only available as a liquid not a foaming spray). One important part of cleaning your vacuum will include cleaning and/or replacing your vacuum’s filter, as Knoll mentions. Many vacuums come with reusable filters, but if you’re due for a new filter and happen to have the Shark Navigator Lift Away, one of the most popular upright vacuums on the market, you should consider this filter replacement. The filter is compatible with more than 20 versions of the Shark Navigator Lift Away, so if you have one, chances are it is compatible. If you’re unsure, you can check the label on the side of your vacuum to make sure the model name matches the list of compatible filters. It includes two HEPA filters, four foam filters and four felt filters which, combined, help sift out dust, pet dander and more, according to the brand. Why do you have to clean a vacuum? It’s important to clean your vacuum regularly because doing so will ultimately help it do its job effectively and for as long as possible. “A vacuum with things stuck in the hose or a dirty filter can really affect how well it works,” says Knoll, who says he and his team go through tons of vacuums. Cleaning your vacuum means more than emptying out the dust bin, too — for a thorough clean, you should also remove, if possible, the brush roll, nozzle, hose, filter, and attachments. How do you clean a vacuum? The steps for cleaning different types of vacuums may vary slightly depending on whether it is an upright, cordless or robot vacuum, but for the most part, many of them have some of the same parts: brush roll, filter, hose and crevice and/or upholstery attachments. Below are some of the most general steps you should take to clean your vacuum. For upright vacuums, unplug the appliance. For cordless and robot vacuums, be sure to remove the battery. Identify the main parts of the vacuum, including the brushroll, filter, suction head, hose, dust bin and attachments. These are the main parts to clean. Some of them are easier to clean if you remove them, while others, like the brush roll, aren’t necessarily, so you don’t have to remove it to clean it, according to Knoll.If possible, find and remove the filter, dust bin and attachments, says Knoll. “Most of these things come apart relatively easily,” he says. “For modern vacuums like Shark, Dyson, and Bissell, you’ll usually have clearly labeled tabs/switches, so you can flip them and remove the dust bin, brush roll, hoses, or filters.”Start with the dust bin. “It’s a little different for each, but for most dust bins, there are two locking clasps on the right and left sides of the bin that you need to flip to remove it,” says Knoll. Manually remove as much debris, dust and dirt as possible and empty it into the trash. Rinse out the dust bin with a small amount of warm water. Spray the inside with a small amount of Dawn Platinum Powerwash Dish Spray, rinse it out again and then dry with a microfiber cloth. Move onto the filter of the vacuum. “The filter usually sits above or under the dust bin. If it’s disposable, toss it and get a new one,” says Knoll. “If it’s reusable (most are these days), add a little drop of mild Dawn dish soap and run some water through it.” It’s extremely important to allow the filter to dry completely before reattaching it and using the vacuum, because it can grow mildew and create odors, according to Knoll. Clean the brush roll, hose and attachments of the vacuum (if applicable). You don’t have to remove the brush roll to make it easier to clean, according to Knoll. “If you turn the vacuum over, you’ll usually see hair wrapped around the brush roll,” says Knoll. “Use scissors to cut between the bristles, then pull the hair out. If you’re having trouble getting the hairs out, cut more, or grab an old hairbrush or a metal tool made for getting hair strands out of bristles, to pull them out.” To clean the hose and attachments, use an object to push out any lodged debris that may be inside. Knoll says he rolls a ping pong ball through the hose to be sure nothing is lodged. Try using something like a long-handled brush, like the Desin Flexible Drain Brush Set, to push debris out of the other end of the hose. After, follow the steps above and rinse it with warm water and a small amount of mild dish soap, and dry it completely before reattaching. How long should a vacuum last? Your vacuum’s longevity heavily depends on how often you use it and how you maintain it. As a professional home cleaner, Knoll says he and his team use vacuums at least three to four times a day, and they last around two years at least, but this is more than the average person. “That said, civilian vacuums used every two to four weeks should easily last three to five years,” he says. “Some traditional upright vacuums can last as long as 10 years. A traditional Sanitaire Tradition upright can last this long.” How do you know when it’s time to replace your vacuum? Before you decide to spend money on another vacuum, it’s important to make sure you’ve done your due diligence when it comes to vacuum maintenance to determine if it’s ready to be thrown out, according to Knoll. “If you clean the filters, remove any clogs, check the brush roll, and it barely picks anything up, it’s probably time to start looking into a new vacuum. Overheating is another sign, or if it repeatedly shuts off,” he says. “This is usually a sign of a failing motor, and the motor is one of the few pieces that are really hard to replace.” How often should you change your vacuum’s filter? It depends on the type of filter, according to Knoll. “Disposable vacuum filters should be changed every six to 12 months,” he says. “For reusable/washable filters, I’d clean them every two to three vacuuming cycles. For foam filters, I’d check them monthly and replace them when they start to break down or no longer clean properly.” Meet our cleaning expert At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Ryan Knoll is a cleaning expert and the owner of home cleaning services company Tidy Casa. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a commerce editor at NBC Selected, where I write about home and kitchen appliances, cleaning, storage and organization and more. I’ve written about how to clean your washer and dryer, hardwood floors, stainless steel appliances, air fryers, coffee makers and even mattresses. I also write about vacuum deals during major sale events like Amazon Prime Day, Black Friday and Cyber Monday. articles.title: US’s RFK Jr claims Arabs ‘don’t produce science’: Why he’s very, very wrong
articles.summary: US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has claimed Arabs have not made contributions to math, science or literature.
articles.body:
United States Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr has sparked uproar with comments he has made denying Arab contributions to mathematics, science and literature.

In a high-voltage rant on Monday, the US health secretary said, “There’s five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don’t produce science. They don’t win the Nobel Prize. They don’t win the Fields Prize. They don’t win the Wolf Prize. They don’t produce literature.”

RFK Jr, who has been involved in anti-vaccine campaigns and has promoted a debunked theory linking vaccines to autism, made the comments during a US election campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan while supporting Republican nominee Mike Rogers, who is up against Arab-American Democrat nominee Abdul El-Sayed, in a tightly contested battle for Michigan’s Senate seat in next week’s midterm elections.

Critics said the comments were racist, Islamophobic and factually inaccurate, pointing to modern and historic Arab innovation in multiple fields.

Here’s how Arabs have made vital contributions to the human understanding of maths, science and literature through the centuries.

Arab contributions to maths, science and humanities

The period known as the Islamic Golden Age, from around 750 AD to 1258 AD, produced many key Arab contributions to medicine at a time when Europe was said to be in its Dark Ages. During this time, Arabic was the language of science and scholarship.

1st-4th centuries: The numerals 0-9, which originated in ancient India, were adopted by Arab mathematicians who spread them across the world. They displaced Roman numerals as a more advanced number system in mathematics.

8th century: Arab and Persian mathematicians were studying the ancient Indian concept of zero in mathematics in Baghdad, long before the Europeans. The number zero was crucial to the development of mathematics – but was absent from widely used Roman numerals in Europe.

813-833: The Arab mathematician Muḥammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi – one of those studying the number 0 – is often referred to as the “father of algebra” as he was the first to treat the method as a separate mathematical discipline in his work, Al-Jabr. This method provided the first linear and quadratic equations, still used as a core part of mathematical study today.

965-1040: Ibn al-Haytham, known as the “father of modern optics”, explained the role that light entering the eye plays in human vision. He was born in Basra in Iraq, but spent most of his working life in Cairo attending to noble families.

936-1013: Abu al-Qasim al-Zahrawi, called “the father of modern surgery”, was considered the greatest surgeon in the Middle Ages. He wrote a 30-volume encyclopaedia detailing medical practices and designed and illustrated many surgical instruments. Born in Azahara, in Andalusia, he was known as Abulcasis in Europe.

9th century: Fatima al-Fihri founded the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco. It is often cited as the oldest continually operating university.

1213-1288: Ibn al-Nafis described pulmonary circulation – the process by which blood passes through the lungs – several centuries before Europeans understood it. He wrote more than 110 volumes of work on surgery, ophthalmology and philosophy while working as a chief physician in Egypt.

915-965: Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi, regarded as the greatest poet in the Arabic language, was Yemeni and grew up immersed in Bedouin Arabic culture. He wrote in classical Arabic and many of his verses became sayings used in everyday Arabic.

1100-1165: Muhammad al-Idrisi was a geographer known for making the Tabula Rogeriana, one of the most accurate and detailed medieval world maps, and a high point of Islamic geography. He was born in Ceuta in Morocco.

In more modern times, RFK Jr’s assertion that Arabs do not win Nobel prizes for science and literature is very far from the truth. Here are some of the highlights:

Peter Medawar won the Nobel Prize for Medicine for work on for work on acquired immune tolerance, which underpins organ transplantation. He was born in Brazil to a Lebanese father.

Michael Atiyah won the Fields Medal, the most prestigious award for mathematics, in 1966. He was born in London to a Lebanese father and Scottish mother. Educated in Egypt, he spent much of his childhood in Cairo and Khartoum.

Egyptian Naguib Mahfouz won the Nobel Prize in Literature for his body of work, including the Cairo Trilogy, which the Swedish Academy said formed “an Arabic narrative art that applies to all mankind”. He is still the only winner of the prize who wrote in Arabic.

Elias James Corey won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for developing retrosynthetic analysis. He is an American of Lebanese descent.

Egyptian Ahmed Zewail won the Wolf Prize for Chemistry. The Wolf Prize is an international award which has been presented to living scientists and artists every year in Israel by the Wolf Foundation since 1978.

Zewail also won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for pioneering femtochemistry, which is the study of chemical reactions on extremely short timescales. He also won the Wolf Prize in Chemistry in 1993.

Egyptian scientist Mohamed ElBaradei shared his Nobel Prize with the International Atomic Energy Agency, which he led.

Omar M Yaghi, born in Jordan to a Palestinian refugee family, won the Wolf Prize in Chemistry in 2018 for work on metal-organic frameworks. He shared the prize with Japan’s Makoto Fujita. The Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) condemned his acceptance of the award because the prize is awarded by an Israeli foundation.

Moungi Bawendi won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for the discovery and synthesis of quantum dots. He was born in France to a Tunisian father, but based in the US.

Yaghi also won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for developing metal-organic frameworks. These are crystalline materials with large internal cavities that can capture and store gases, harvest water from air, and trap pollutants. He shared the prize with Susumu Kitagawa from Japan and Richard Robson from Australia.

In a post on X, vaccine scientist Peter Hotez of the Texas Medical Center weighed in on historical Arab scholarship, saying, “It was the Arab scientists of the Middle Ages who kept Aristotle, Hippocrates, Galen alive to hand it down in the Renaissance.”

Broadcaster Mehdi Hasan described RFK Jr’s comments as “racist” and, in a post on X, wrote: “One of the men who won the Nobel Prize for Chemistry last year was a Palestinian-American, Omar Yaghi.”

The Council on American-Islamic Relations called for the US health secretary to be removed. It said: “To stand on a public stage as a sitting US cabinet official and dehumanise half a billion people – and millions of Muslim and Christian Arab Americans – with fabricated, white supremacist talking points is utterly disqualifying for public office. His sweeping erasure of Arab contributions to humanity is not only maliciously false, but it also fans the flames of anti-Arab and anti-Muslim hate at a time when communities are already vulnerable to bigoted attacks from other public officials nationwide.”

articles.title: More cats abandoned 'due to rising costs' says Coventry RSPCA
articles.summary: The shelter has seen a "huge increase" in the number of cats it has taken in, compared to last year.
articles.body:
An animal charity has said the cost of caring for pets is among reasons for a "huge increase" in the number of cats and kittens being taken in by its centre.

RSPCA Coventry and District Branch said it cared for 399 cats and kittens over the summer, which was 150 more than the same time last year.

Emma Davies of the centre said: "We think a lot of that is down to rising costs," adding it included the cost of neutering pets, which in turn resulted in more kittens being born.

Nationally, the RSPCA has warned of a "cat crisis" and said it is now caring for more felines than dogs, adding that the influxes have put pressure on its centres.

The site in Coundon Wedge Drive, Coventry, is run independently to the national RSPCA and said it costs £40,000 a month to run the shelter.

It is currently full with 80 cats, but the centre told the BBC that there is also a waiting list of 130 people who are having to give up their pets.

Davies said: "If your cat is older and perhaps has a health condition, insurance for that and covering vet costs can also be expensive".

"So we are finding that a lot of people are looking to us to surrender their animal because they can no longer afford to take care of it," she said.

"We have unfortunately had quite a few abandonments at the centre, in terms of kittens left in cardboard boxes, cats left in carrier bags and things like that."

Staff also believe an increase in the number of people breeding cats may also be pushing up the number of rescues.

Davies advised anyone struggling to talk to the RSPCA to see if they can help, such as with pet food provision or by treating cats at its own vet clinic.

Beth Clements, RSPCA assistant director of animal services, said nationally it had seen "a huge influx of cats and kittens".

"Sadly it just isn't slowing down and it's having a massive impact on our centres and branches," she said.

"So far this year we're taking in an average of 624 cats each month across our 14 national centres and private boarding establishments.

"That's not including the massive numbers our independent local branch network are taking in too."

articles.title: In 2026, a Minnesota grower travelled 35 hours with a 2,389-pound pumpkin and won California’s weigh-off for the fifth time
articles.summary: Travis Gienger from Minnesota achieved victory at Half Moon Bay’s 53rd Safeway World Championship with his impressive 2,389-pound pumpkin named Rocky, earning him $21,501. This win marks his fifth championship as records continue to break for giant pumpkins.
articles.body: A horticulture teacher by the name of Travis Gienger, from Anoka, Minnesota, won the top award at Half Moon Bay’s 53rd Safeway World Championship on October 12, 2026. Gienger’s pumpkin, called Rocky, weighed in at 2,389 pounds and earned him $21,501, based on the contest’s payout system of $9 for each pound.The competition drew dozens of growers to Half Moon Bay, who brought their giant pumpkins. According to the official results, Gienger won the Open Division, and the second position was taken by Jake Leonard of Rocklin, California, who finished with 2,273 pounds and received $3,000, alongside a $1,000 award for the largest Californian pumpkin. For third place, Brian Christensen of Rexburg, Idaho, came in at 1,873 pounds. Rocky was transported from Minnesota in a journey that took about 35 hours, with Gienger and his family driving, the Associated Press said. The pumpkin was roughly the size of a small car, and after the win, Gienger said: “Five-time champion, that’s what we came here to do.”Rocky’s growth and the return to Half Moon BayGienger started growing Rocky in April in his backyard patch in Anoka and, CBS Minnesota reported, he spent the summer weeding, trimming, fertilising and feeding the pumpkin sugar water. The giant pumpkins were capable of gaining 60 to 70 pounds in a day, Gienger said, and Rocky had added nearly 1,700 pounds during July.The growing season brought temperatures below freezing, and to cope with it, Gienger said he will likely need a climate-controlled environment if he wants to compete more seriously. The conditions had made growing Rocky particularly challenging, but the pumpkin continued developing through the Minnesota summer.Gienger’s return to the stage in 2026 came after a year of missing out on Half Moon Bay. His three-year winning streak from 2022 to 2024 had ended in 2025, when his pumpkin broke while growing, though he had previously won in 2020. Following the competition, Gienger posed with his championship rings, per the official results, and organisers built a float for him in the Half Moon Bay parade. Rocky was showcased in the downtown parade the weekend after the weigh-off.The records, awards and other growers At the 2026 Half Moon Bay event, Rocky was the heaviest pumpkin, but it remained below Gienger’s own contest record. In 2023, his 2,749-pound pumpkin, named Michael Jordan, had set the weigh-off mark. Subsequently, Guinness World Records recognised the pumpkin that measured 253 inches around as the largest jack-o’-lantern after artist Eric Jones carved it in Clarence, New York, in November 2023.In the days before the California competition, the wider record had changed. Fox 9 reported that on October 3, Ian Paton, a British grower, had set a 2,856-pound record that stood for only a few days. Ron Wallace’s pumpkin followed, weighing 3,156 pounds at a Rhode Island weigh-off on October 10, though Guinness had not yet verified it. Gienger missed out on Half Moon Bay’s additional $30,000 award for breaking the world record, the AP noted.The weigh-off itself began in 1974 as a friendly challenge between Half Moon Bay and Circleville, Ohio, to see who could grow the biggest pumpkin. Other growers beyond the main weigh-off standings were also recognised by the competition, such as Tom McGuirk of Half Moon Bay, who won the Coastside-grown pumpkin award with a 352-pound entry. Vince Zunino of Los Altos Hills also received the Joe Cotchett family award for the prettiest pumpkin, named Tinkerbell.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Serial killer Ted Bundy linked to teenage girl's murder after 52 years
articles.summary: Authorities in Utah used advanced DNA technology to solve the cold case decades after the notorious killer was executed.
articles.body:
Authorities in Utah have used advanced DNA technology to link notorious serial killer Ted Bundy to the murder of a 17-year-old girl whose body was discovered by hunters 52 years ago.

Melissa Ann Smith, the daughter of a local police chief, was found on 27 October 1974 with signs of rape and torture.

In April, Utah officials identified teenager Laura Ann Aime as another of Bundy's victims. Evidence gathered from that case was subsequently used to help solve Smith's case.

Before his death by execution in 1989, Bundy had confessed to killing two other teenage girls in Utah. He has been linked to at least 30 murders across the US.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Utah County Sgt Mike Reynolds said there were more Bundy cases still being examined in the state. "With every case closure may we stomp the memory of Ted Bundy out," he said.

Salt Lake County Sheriff Rosie Rivera added that the case should be a sign to other cold case victims "that there is hope out there".

"Every single day forensics is changing and we have the ability to take a look at these cases again and again," she said.

She also praised detectives for preserving evidence from the case for so long, saying it "demonstrates the need to preserve evidence even when decades pass".

In April, the director of the Utah Bureau of Forensic Services told the Salt Lake Tribune, there were 444 unsolved death investigations in the state, including 258 homicides.

Bundy is among America's most infamous serial killers, and began his spree by attacking victims throughout the US Pacific north-west.

Known to often approach women in public places, he would gain their trust with his charm or a fake injury, and then lure them to secluded areas and kill them.

He was first arrested in 1975 for kidnapping a woman and sentenced to 15 years in jail. But in 1977 he escaped by jumping out of a prison library window.

He was recaptured for eight days and then escaped again, continuing to kill until he was finally caught in 1978.

articles.title: After ACL setback, FC Goa look to turn the corner
articles.summary: Panaji: Gouramangi Singh feels it’s “just a matter of time” before the results start showing at FC Goa.
articles.body: Panaji: Gouramangi Singh feels it’s “just a matter of time” before the results start showing at FC Goa.Since the start of the season, Goa have won just one of their five competitive matches, four of them in Asian football. Their only game in the Indian Super League (ISL) ended in a draw against Chennaiyin FC, who have lost two of their three games and have only a point. Now, they return to domestic football. But even though there are question marks over the team’s ability to entertain, grind out results, and match the teams of old, coach Gouramangi has called for patience.“Of course, when it comes to results, there are no excuses, but this is a new team with several players making their debuts in the top tier,” Gouramangi told TOI on Tuesday. “I have no complaints about what the boys did in the ACL (AFC Challenge League). They showed a desire to win, and tried hard too. Let’s remember this is a new team. I would have been worried if the boys are not feeling good about each other or they're not feeling good about what we are trying to do as a team. Then it would be a bad moment for me.”After the unexpected AFC Challenge League (ACL) group-stage exit, Goa will be put to test against SC Delhi at the Nehru Stadium in Fatorda on Wednesday.The visitors are at the bottom of the pool after losing both games, but nobody will be fooled by looking at just the points table. In both games, Delhi were hugely competitive and had some brilliant moments against much stronger sides like Mohun Bagan SG and Bengaluru FC.“They may have lost both games, but they were good. They were leading but could not hold on (to the leads). That’s football. We too have learned our lessons in Kuwait. We want to go out there and win,” said Gouramangi.Five Goa players were either unavailable or not fully fit for the concluding ACL group-stage clash against Qadsia SC last week. The good news is that at least three of them – Prachit Gaonkar, Bob Raj and Isak Vanlalruatfela – have recovered and are available for selection, while Aakash Sangwan and Harsh Patre will need time to regain full fitness.“The ten days in Kuwait where we spent time together, suffered on the field, understood each other (better) helped. The team is improving. I agree the results are not there but there are good things that do not always show up. For us, it’s important to win against Delhi. The boys are up for the challenge,” said Gouramangi.Despite two losses in a row, Delhi have been hugely competitive with coach Tomasz Tchorz confident in his side’s abilities.“I am very happy with the performance of the team,” Tchorz. “I think we played a very good game (against Bagan). We repeated what was a very good first half performance in Bengaluru. articles.title: Tanzania’s jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu ends brief hunger strike
articles.summary: Lissu, who faces treason charge carrying a possible death sentence, refused food after being denied access to lawyers.
articles.body:
Tanzania’s jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu has ended a brief hunger strike after prison authorities allowed him to meet privately with his lawyers, his lawyer has said.

Lissu, who leads the opposition’s Party for Democracy and Progress (CHADEMA) ‌and came second in the 2020 presidential election, began refusing food on Monday after his lawyers were denied entry to the prison where he is being held, party spokesperson Brenda Rupia wrote on X.

“Lissu did not take his tea, breakfast or lunch,” his lawyer Rugemeleza Nshala told The Associated Press on Tuesday. Nshala said Lissu ended the strike after lunchtime, following the meeting with his brother.

His detention, along with the alleged abductions of ⁠government critics, has led to scrutiny of the human rights record of President Samia Suluhu Hassan, who won a 2025 election.

The government has rejected accusations of ⁠widespread abuses and said it is committed to respecting human rights. It ordered an investigation into reports of abductions in 2024, though no official findings have been made public.

Accounts of Lissu’s protest have differed. While CHADEMA spokesperson Rupia said on X that Lissu began refusing food on Monday, Nshala told AP that the strike began on Tuesday morning, after promised private consultations failed to take place.

Tanzania’s prisons service denied the reports, telling the Swahili-language daily Mwananchi that Lissu was safe and was not on hunger strike.

Nshala had raised concerns about Lissu’s health, saying he relies on medication.

Lissu survived being shot 16 times in a 2017 assassination attempt. He was arrested in April 2025 after addressing a rally calling for electoral reforms, and was charged with treason over what prosecutors said was a speech urging the public to rebel and disrupt last year’s general election.

He has pleaded not guilty, and his lawyers say the charges are politically motivated. A judgement is due on November 6.

On Tuesday, CHADEMA announced seven days of mourning, from Thursday to November 4, to mark the anniversary of the October 29 election. A government-appointed inquiry found that at least 518 people were killed in the violence that followed the vote. CHADEMA puts the death toll at about 2,000, a figure the United Nations said it could not verify.

articles.title: Florida mom arrested after leaving 4 kids home alone during dayslong trip to Vegas
articles.summary: A Florida mom was arrested and charged with child neglect after she left her four kids home alone for nearly three days while she was in Las Vegas, the local sheriff reported Monday.
articles.body: A Florida mom was arrested and charged with child neglect after she left her four kids home alone for nearly three days while she was in Las Vegas, the local sheriff reported Monday. Irene Miller was busted after a dispatcher received a 911 call on Oct. 21 from one of the kids in the Kissimmee home who reported “that her 9-year-old brother had been injured by a dumbbell that fell on his head,” the Osceola County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement. When the deputies arrived at the residence, they found four children ages 14, 12, 11 and 9 — and no adults watching over them. While paramedics took the injured boy to a nearby hospital for treatment of what turned out to be an apparently minor injury, the deputies tracked Miller down by telephone. “She told the deputy that she was working in Las Vegas and would return on October 23, 2026,” the sheriff’s statement said. “Deputies learned that Mrs. Miller had left for Las Vegas on October 18, 2026.” Miller, according to the statement, told deputies that she had a babysitter coming from Tampa in the mornings to get the children ready for school and to check on them after school. Kissimmee is located near Orlando and about 70 miles east of Tampa. Miller also said she did not insist that the babysitter stay the night at the house with the children, the statement said. While the children were taken to their father’s home, sheriff’s detectives were dispatched “to meet Irene Miller as she exited her flight from Las Vegas on Friday morning,” the statement said. Miller, 50, was charged with four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm and booked into the Orange County jail. As of Monday, a search of jail records showed that she was no longer behind bars. ​“The Osceola County Sheriff’s Office will not tolerate child neglect,” said Sheriff Chris Blackmon. “These cases will be investigated, and charges will be brought against the parents who are not properly supervising or caring for their children.”

articles.title: Israelis vote in record numbers in first national election since the Oct. 7 Hamas massacre
articles.summary: Israel election exit polls show Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar locked in a fight with neither bloc reaching 61 Knesset seats.
articles.body: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israelis turned out in exceptionally high numbers Tuesday for the country’s first national election since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacre, with initial exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud emerging as the largest party but his governing coalition falling short of a parliamentary majority, potentially opening the door to a change in leadership. The projections released by Israel’s three major television networks after polls closed at 10 p.m. local time (4 p.m. ET) showed Likud winning 25 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 23 seats for former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party in Channels 12 and 13 exit polls, and 21 seats according to Kan 11. The projected parliamentary balance showed 50 seats for Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc, 53 for the main opposition parties and 17 for Arab parties, leaving neither major bloc with the 61 seats generally needed to form a government. Although Netanyahu’s party is projected to remain the largest in parliament, his political future is far from secure. The opposition parties, together with the Arab factions, would hold a combined 70 seats, although that does not mean they would necessarily agree to form a government together. FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER The results set the stage for potentially weeks of coalition negotiations, with the possibility that Netanyahu could lose power despite Likud finishing first. Netanyahu fights for political future as Israel heads to polls with Iran threat looming The results are preliminary projections, not an official vote count, and could change as ballots are tallied in the coming days. The election followed an extraordinary day at polling stations across Israel, with long lines and voter participation reaching levels not seen in decades. Israeli voter turnout surged to a historic high, with 55.7% of eligible voters casting their ballots by 4 p.m. local time (10 a.m. ET), according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. The figure marked the highest turnout recorded at that hour since measurements began in 1973, underscoring the intensity of the country's national election. The unusually high participation prompted election officials to streamline voting procedures and assure voters that anyone arriving at a polling station before the 10 p.m. deadline would be allowed to cast a ballot. The vote was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu's leadership following three years of war and continuing questions about responsibility for the security failures that allowed Hamas terrorists to kill approximately 1,200 people and abduct 251 others on Oct. 7, 2023. JD VANCE DECLINES TO ENDORSE NETANYAHU DESPITE TRUMP'S STRONG BACKING Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, campaigned on his record of confronting Iran and its regional proxies, highlighting Israel's military achievements and his relationship with President Donald Trump.His opponents accused him of failing to accept responsibility for the October 7 security failures and opposed his government's approach to investigating the failures that preceded the massacre. A last-minute battle for every vote Throughout the final hours of the campaign, Netanyahu, Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and other party leaders mounted an intensive effort to mobilize supporters and win over undecided voters. Netanyahu's Likud party prepared hundreds of targeted campaign videos and social media messages, making digital outreach a central part of its last-minute election strategy. Eisenkot's campaign pushed supporters to rally behind Yashar as the leading alternative to Likud, while Bennett traveled between cities and engaged voters directly and through WhatsApp conversations. NETANYAHU FIGHTS FOR POLITICAL FUTURE AS ISRAEL HEADS TO POLLS WITH IRAN THREAT LOOMING The campaign's closing hours also featured personal appeals, phone calls to undecided voters and aggressive turnout operations across the political spectrum. The final days were particularly important because a relatively small share of voters remained undecided about which party to support. A Times of Israel poll published five days before the election found that 87% of respondents had already made their final choice, while 2.4% remained undecided between the pro- and anti-Netanyahu political blocs. Other surveys suggested a larger pool of undecided voters, although many were choosing between parties within the same political camp rather than switching sides. That distinction could prove decisive in Israel's parliamentary system, where political parties need at least 3.25% of valid votes to enter the 120-seat Knesset. Even a slight change in the vote share of smaller parties could shift several parliamentary seats and determine whether either camp has a realistic path to power. TRUMP SAYS NETANYAHU NEEDS TO BE RE-ELECTED, OR ELSE US WILL HAVE TO 'FINISH THE JOB’ AGAINST IRAN ALONE What happens next? Despite the exit poll projections, the identity of Israel's next prime minister may remain uncertain for weeks. Unlike in the United States, Israelis vote for political parties rather than directly electing their head of government. The 120 seats in parliament are allocated proportionally, and parties must secure at least 3.25% of valid votes to win representation. Once the final results are certified, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will consult with the newly elected political factions and select the lawmaker he believes has the strongest chance of forming a government. That candidate will have 28 days to negotiate a governing coalition, with the possibility of a 14-day extension. articles.title: After Behala naked mob justice, cops parade 3 accused semi-naked to ‘reconstruct crime’
articles.summary: Kolkata police paraded three accused shirtless and barefoot at Behala crime spot after teens were forced to walk naked; rights groups question legality.
articles.body: Kolkata: Thirty-six hours after an 18-year-old, his father and the youth’s friend were forced to walk naked at gunpoint in Behala’s Sarsuna by family members of a 13-year-old girl as punishment for the teen allegedly kissing her, cops on Tuesday paraded three of the accused shirtless and barefoot at the same spot, claiming they were “recreating the crime scene”.The three men — father of the minor girl, her maternal uncle and a friend of the uncle — were brought to Khudiram Pally Manasatala in a police SUV. With ropes tied around their waists, they were made to walk semi-naked over 100 metres as residents lined both sides of the road, many filming the scene. Police and paramilitary personnel formed a human chain to prevent attacks by angry neighbours. The fourth accused in the case is the girl’s mother.While the girl’s parent and uncle were arrested on Monday, the uncle’s friend, Shankar Shaw, was nabbed early Tuesday. Cops are probing if he alerted the girl’s family after allegedly spotting the couple kissing and provided the firearm used to threaten the victims.“At least five others, and even those who shot videos of the three men being forced to walk naked, are under the lens. Raids are on to nab them,” said a senior officer, who declined to elaborate on the “recreation of crime”.In June, Calcutta High Court had observed that police may arrest an accused but cannot deliberately humiliate them. “Under the guise of arrest, the police cannot intentionally disgrace the accused,” the bench had said.Human rights group APDR questioned the police action. Its general secretary Altaf Ahmed said, “Where in police procedure is this allowed? Is it written in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita? The police are supposed to uphold the law… not take the law into their own hands.”According to the police complaint, the 18-year-old and his friend were dragged to the girl’s house on Sunday after the couple were spotted together. The boy’s father was then summoned and allegedly assaulted.The 18-year-old told newspersons on Tuesday that his girlfriend had called him on Sunday saying she wanted to meet. “I was talking to her and holding her hand when suddenly her maternal uncle’s friend grabbed me by the collar. Then her uncle and her father arrived. They grabbed my friend too and forced us into a car. They gave my father three choices — either shoot me, stab me, or frame me in a false rape case. Otherwise, they said they would strip me and parade me around.” He added, “Love is not a crime. Why was I punished for it?”His father said he was severely assaulted in the presence of other people and then asked to kill his son. “They had a pistol with them. I had no choice but to agree to walk naked through the road. articles.title: King acknowledges 'suffering of the past' as Caribbean tour begins
articles.summary: The King is on a nine-day tour that will take him to three countries, including the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda.
articles.body:
King Charles has arrived in the Bahamas for a nine-day tour of the Caribbean - the first time he has visited the region as monarch.

The King, wearing sunglasses and a grey suit, was given a ceremonial welcome at the airport and was greeted by the island's Governor General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt and its Prime Minister Philip Edward.

He spoke with members of the Royal Bahamian Defence Force as he inspected a Guard of Honour on the runway.

Buckingham Palace says the King will not shy away from "colonial legacy" and the impact of the slave trade during the visit but, in line with the UK government position, he will not apologise for Britain's role in the slave trade.

Nor will he offer reparations - compensation from countries that took part in the slave trade.

His first engagement is at a youth rally at Clifford Park where the King attended the island's independence celebrations as Prince of Wales in 1973.

The King is also expected to address his 50-year-long commitment to fighting climate change, highlighting the challenges faced by low-lying Caribbean islands, saying that "our world cries out for healing".

And he will call on the young people at the rally to "take up the sacred task to play your part" as "in years to come, this will be surely be the measure of every person - how they answered the call to care for planet earth - the source of our life, our prosperity and our security."

Buckingham Palace says opportunities for the King to reflect on the legacy of the slave trade will be built into his schedule in all three countries with visits planned to memorials and other places of reflection and remembrance.

A spokesperson for the palace tells the BBC that the King's programme on the tour "will primarily focus on shining a light on the many modern partnerships and opportunities for the future", specifically those which are "having a transformative effect on the region".

For the King, the spokesperson added, the "tour is both a new journey but also the continuance of a lifelong one, in which he has sought to engage, understand and educate about the most shameful aspects of our past".

Those themes will be reflected by the King through the nine-day visit, the palace said.

The visit has been planned alongside the governments of the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda with an emphasis on honouring the past but also looking forward to the ambition and possibility for future generations.

The King will move to Guyana later this week where his engagements will focus on the environment and biodiversity.

He will then visit Antigua and Barbuda, where he will be joined by Queen Camilla, for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) and his keynote speech as leader of the Commonwealth.

CHOGM is a biennial summit which brings together leaders of 56 Commonwealth countries to address shared challenges and advance cooperation.

articles.title: Exit polls following Israeli elections indicate no clear winner
articles.summary: The official results are due to be published on November 4, more than a week after the vote.
articles.body:
Exit polls following what many pundits and voters have billed as the most pivotal election in Israel’s history indicate no clear winner in the hard-fought contest.

According to exit polls, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc is projected to secure 50 seats, while the bloc led by opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot is expected to win 52 or 53 seats. Sixty-one seats are needed to form a majority government. Arab parties are projected to collectively win 18 seats.

Polling stations closed at 10pm (20:00 GMT) local time. Preliminary results are expected on Wednesday, followed by a final tally on Friday. The official results are due to be published on November 4, eight days after the vote.

Exit polls are based on interviews with voters immediately after they have cast their ballots. The interviews help project the election’s outcome and have in previous elections tended to anticipate the results closely.

Voter turnout in the Israeli election reached 74.3 percent as of 8pm (18:00 GMT), according to data released by the Central Elections Committee. By comparison, turnout in the 2022 election was 70.63 percent.

Polls predicted a tight race between incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and leading opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party and a former army chief.

Israel’s Central Elections Committee rejected a request by Netanyahu’s Likud Party to extend voting hours.

The election is the first since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza three years ago, following Hamas-led attacks on the country, and is widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s handling of the events on October 7, 2023 and the conflicts that followed.

L’Occitane’s Advent calendar comes with 24 of the brand’s bestselling body and hair care products, including its popular shower oil, exfoliating shower gel, fragrance and more in a perfect sample size. All 12 products are full-size, so you can discover viral favorites like the Telescopic Mascara, Infallible Blurfection Powder, Color Riche Lipstick and Infallible Setting Spray in one place. If you never leave home without a lip balm and have one in every bag you own, you need this Burt’s Bees Advent calendar. It comes with 12 lip balms in flavors like sugar cookie, cinnamon apple crisp, vanilla bean and peppermint bark. Each lip balm has beeswax and vitamin E to soften and hydrate skin all day, according to the brand. This Advent calendar comes with 24 Sephora-brand skin care, makeup, beauty tools and bath products. You’ll get 13 full-size and five travel-size blushes, face masks, mascaras, eye creams and more, plus six accessories like a makeup sponge and hair clips. I love using Laneige’s popular K-beauty products every day, and if you’re looking to try bestsellers beyond the brand’s viral lip mask, this Advent calendar is filled with 12 full and mini sizes. You get face masks, moisturizer, cleanser, serums and lip balms, all of which have soothing and hydrating ingredients like peptides, hyaluronic acid and ceramides. There’s travel sizes of the viral Libre and Black Opium eau de parfums, as well as a mini Lash Clash Mascara, a Loveshine Lip Oil Stick and much more. Everything is packaged in a gorgeous keepsake box, too. You’ll also get multiple toner pads, a cleanser, a liquid blush and other products to help brighten and hydrate the skin. This 25-day Advent calendar comes with exclusives and year-round favorites, including Sticky Dates Shower Gel and Dream Cream Body Lotion. The products all come packaged in a festive, reusable wicker basket. If you’re looking for something smaller, consider Lush’s 12 Days of Christmas Advent Calendar. The limited-edition gift set comes with 12 of the brand’s most popular products, including The Rich Cream and The Cream Cleansing Gel, all neatly packaged in its signature royal blue tiered box. It also includes a dermaplaning set for your face, hair clips, scrunches, a bonnet, hair perfume and shampoo and conditioner bars. Best fragrance Advent calendars When it comes to luxury fragrances, the best thing you can do is snag a collection of sample sizes to try out all of the scents. This 25-day Jo Malone Advent calendar lets you do exactly that. It comes with a variety of fragrances and colognes, plus candles, body creams, soaps, hand creams and other body care products, in 18 scents. Plus, everything is individually wrapped inside a festive, multi-drawer box. This is one of the most visually stunning Advent calendars on this list; it has a festive, illustrated townhouse design with 24 individual doors and windows, each of which reveal a bestseller across home fragrance, perfumes and body care. You’ll get candles, hand creams, body washes and more from some of the brand’s most popular scents, plus keepsakes like a 2026 Christmas ornament and a hand cream tube key. You can also try out the brand’s 12 Days of Luxury calendar for a smaller assortment. If you’re looking to try out goodies from across the DedCool universe, this Advent calendar comes with 12 products from its fragrance, laundry, body and home collections. Best nail care Advent calendars Dazzle Dry’s Advent calendar comes with everything you need to prep, paint, finish and touch up your gel manicure without needing a UV or LED light. You get two exclusive full-size nail polish shades and two sparkly minis, which are quick-drying and last for up to two weeks, according to the brand. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans loves how rich and long-lasting the colors are. “This was my first time using Dazzle Dry and, as an at-home manicure girlie, it was a fantastic intro to the brand,” she says. “I’m conflicted because I want to share this with my mother because I know she’ll love it — she also does her own nails — but I also want to keep all of it for myself.” Level up your at-home manicures with this Advent calendar, which comes with 11 exclusive full-size Olive & June nail polishes in multiple shades. This calendar also includes two types of top coats: Sparkle Fairy Top Coat, which has a glowy, iridescent finish, and Long-Lasting Top Coat, which has a glossy finish. Every option on my final list comes from a brand we’ve previously covered or have personally tried. Some of the calendars were also sent to us as courtesy samples from brands for testing or ones we bought with our own money. To evaluate each one, I assessed its contents, price and packaging.
